Grand Master’s Decisions
Grand Master Cooper’s Decision No. 1
Clarifies Confidentiality of Lodge Records
Under Section 804.840 of the California Masonic Code, it is the
duty of every Mason to maintain the confidentiality of Lodge transactions. No
proceeding of the Lodge not proper to be made public shall be disclosed, either
directly or indirectly, to any person not otherwise entitled to the same. While
this is a long standing rule in our Grand Lodge, exceptions have been allowed.
For example, there is authority from 1871 and 1914 allowing audits of lodge
books by a Master Mason in good standing of another lodge. See Section 493h
of the 1956 California Masonic Code. There is also a 1972 authority authorizing
disclosure to a government auditor of lodge books but only to the extent that they
are being audited. See Section 2548h of the 1975 California Masonic Code. I
do know that some lodges use outside CPA’s to do their tax returns. In my view,
Constituent Lodges may disclose to a non-Mason information about the Lodge’s
transactions to the extent necessary to assist the Lodge in tax return preparation,
preparation of financial statements and their audits, provided that the non-Mason
sign a confidentiality agreement before receiving the disclosure to guard against
prohibited public disclosure.
It is my decision that Constituent Lodges may disclose to a non-Mason
information about the Lodge’s transactions to the extent necessary to assist the
Lodge in tax return preparation, preparation of financial statements and their
audits, provided that the non-Mason sign a confidentiality agreement before
receiving the disclosure.
If you agree with this interpretation of our law, I ask you to vote “yes”
for Grand Master’s Decision No. 1.
If you approve this decision, the following narrative will be added
to the appendix of the California Masonic Code in which the Grand Master’s
interpretative decisions are recorded:
Interpretation of Section 804.840 of the California Masonic Code.
Confidentiality of Lodge Records
(2014 G.M. Decision No. 1)
Constituent Lodges may disclose to a non-Mason information about the Lodge’s
transactions to the extent necessary to assist the Lodge in tax return preparation,
preparation of financial statements and their audits, provided that the non-Mason
sign a confidentiality agreement before receiving the disclosure.

166

Proceedings of the

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
It is the policy of this Grand Lodge to ensure that Constituent Lodges
obey not only the laws, rules, and regulations governing Freemasonry, but also
obey the civil laws of the jurisdiction in which they are situated. All Lodges
must prepare tax returns and other financial documents to help ensure these
civil laws are followed. It is often beyond the skills of Lodge members to
prepare accurate financial documents and they find it would be beneficial to
engage a non-Masonically affiliated person or entity to prepare these documents.
However, under the California Masonic Code, the confidentiality of Lodge
transactions must be maintained. Grand Master Cooper’s Decision Number 1
notes that on various occasions this confidentiality rule has been modified in
connection with Lodge finances. The Grand Master’s determination that Lodge
transactions may be disclosed to a non-Mason “to the extent necessary to assist
the Lodge in tax return preparation, preparation of financial statements and their
audits” is in line with the prior modifications of our confidentiality provisions.
This Decision ensures that the business of a Lodge remain confidential by
requiring a third party to sign a non-disclosure agreement before receiving
Lodge transactional data.
This determination is consistent with the policy and general purposes
of this Grand Lodge.
Decision AFFIRMED.

Grand Master Cooper’s Decision No. 2
Clarifies Ownership of Cemetery, Burial Plots and Burial Rights
From the first founding of Masonic Lodges in California, Lodges
established cemeteries for the burial of their deceased members, or the deceased
wives, widows and orphans of such members. As an act of Masonic charity, the
purchase and maintenance of Masonic cemeteries, burial plots and burial rights
were considered a primary duty of Masons for those in need. As time went on,
some Masonic cemeteries, burial plots and burial rights were placed under the
ownership of Hall Associations on the analogy that all such property should be
owned through these autonomous associations. I do not believe that our California
Masonic Code allows Hall Associations to own cemetery property, burial plots or
burial rights.
Under Section 900.010 of the Code, a Lodge may use an incorporated
Masonic Hall Association for the purpose of purchasing, erecting or maintaining
and holding title to real estate for a building for Lodge uses and purposes. A
Masonic Hall Association may collect income from this real estate and turn over

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

167

the entire amount thereof, less expenses, to its members or shareholders. There is
no authority in the Code for the Hall Association to hold any other assets, other
than real estate for a building for Lodge uses and purposes and related assets,
including the funds necessary for its operations.
Rulings of the United States Internal Revenue Service suggest that
entities with the tax exemption of our Hall Associations may only (1) operate real
property housing operations of the nonprofit parent and/or third party tenants and
(2) hold investment funds for the nonprofit parent. Holding cemeteries or burial
plots is not a purpose which the IRS has sanctioned and may result in a loss of
nonprofit status.
It is therefore my decision that a Masonic Hall Association may not hold
or administer any assets, other than real estate for a building for Lodge uses and
purposes and related assets, including the funds necessary for the Association’s
operations. I encourage succeeding Grand Masters to allow Masonic Hall
Associations two years from the close of this Annual Communication to come
into compliance with this decision by transferring title to all cemeteries, burial
plots and burial rights to the Lodge or other third parties.
If you agree with this interpretation of our law, I ask you to vote “yes”
for Grand Master’s Decision No. 2.
If you approve this decision, the following narrative will be added
to the appendix of the California Masonic Code in which the Grand Master’s
interpretative decisions are recorded:
Interpretation of Sections 900.010 and 809.140.A.4 of the California
Masonic Code.
Hall Association Assets
(2014 G.M. Decision No. 2)
A Masonic Hall Association may not hold or administer any assets, other than real
estate for a building for Lodge uses and purposes and related assets, including the
funds necessary for the Association’s operations.
Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
Over the years, the California Masonic Code has been carefully written
to avoid any potential conflicts that could result in a loss of our tax exempt
status. Section 900.010 of the California Masonic Code specifically limits the
real property that a Masonic Hall Association can own to the lodge building
and land. Based on this wording, the Grand Master made a decision that a Hall
Association could not own cemetery property.

168

Proceedings of the

It should be noted that Section 809.140.A.4 seems to imply that, with
the consent of Grand Lodge, a Masonic Hall Association may own other real
property. However, cemetery properties that are being held to preserve future
interment rights are not viewed as real properties, but rather as intangible
personal property rights. As such, a Masonic Hall Association cannot own
these interment sites and, in order to protect our tax exempt status, Grand
Lodge would not approve such an arrangement.
On the other hand, such property can be owned by individual lodges
as long as the intent is to promote fraternal purposes. In fact, the lodge would
be holding the cemetery property in order to facilitate burial rights.
Grand Master Cooper’s Decision 14-02 is consistent with the policy
and general purposes of this Grand Lodge.
Decision AFFIRMED.

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

169

Grand Master’s Recommendation
Grand Master Cooper’s Recommendation No. 1
Creates Board President Tenure
The concept of rotation in office is an ancient Masonic practice. It is
embedded in our California Masonic Code with most positions as appointive
Grand Lodge Officers, inspectors, board members and committee members
limited to nine years. In addition, the code limits service as the chairman of a
Grand Lodge committee to a maximum of five years.
The presidents of our constitutional boards are not subject to the
same five-year limit as committee chairman. They should be. It is therefore my
recommendation that the California Masonic Code be amended to provide that
the president of a constitutional board may only serve a maximum of five years
at one time.
If you adopt this recommendation, the following changes will be made
to the Code. Section 500.040 of the Code would be amended to read as marked:
§500.040. MANAGEMENT.
The Bylaws of this corporation shall provide the following:
A.

The officers of this corporation shall be a President, a Vice President, a
Chief Financial Officer and a Secretary. This corporation may also have,
at the discretion of the Board, such other officers as may be provided in its
Bylaws. The President and Vice President shall be elected by the Board of
Trustees of this corporation from its membership each year, at the close
of the Annual Communication. If a member of the Board of Trustees has
served as President for five consecutive years, he shall be ineligible for
election as President until the lapse of one year;

B.

The President shall be the chief executive officer of this corporation and
shall preside at all meetings of the Board of Trustees. In the absence or
disability of the President, the Vice President shall perform all the duties of
the President and when so acting shall have all the powers of the President;

C.

The Grand Treasurer shall serve ex-officio as the Chief Financial
Officer of this corporation but his duties shall not require that he attend
each meeting of this corporation’s Board of Trustees. He shall keep an
accurate, complete and uniform set of financial records, accounting for
all receipts, disbursements, assets and liabilities of this corporation. Such
records shall be kept on the accrual basis of accounting and maintained
in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. The
financial statements of this corporation shall be prepared in accordance
with general accepted accounting principles on the accrual basis of

170

Proceedings of the
accounting, using a fiscal year as may be selected by the Grand Treasurer
in consultation with the Board of Trustees. The Grand Treasurer shall
prepare and deliver, at each Annual Communication, a detailed report of
the financial condition of this corporation prepared in accordance with
generally accepted accounting principles;

D.

The Grand Secretary shall serve ex-officio as the Secretary of this
corporation but his duties shall not require that he attend each meeting
of this corporation’s Board of Trustees to record the Board’s minutes.
He shall maintain files of all minutes of such Board, taken by him
or his designee, in a safe place in the Grand Lodge office. He shall
supervise, subject to the ultimate control of the Board of Trustees of
this corporation, all clerical, administrative or accounting personnel
employed by or assigned to this corporation, whose offices are within the
Grand Lodge office. He shall secure from a reputable casualty company
and maintain in force a blanket fidelity insurance covering all officers
of this corporation under principles substantially similar to the rules
provided in Section 407.085 of this Code;

E.

The Board shall maintain an office in the same building and in connection
with offices of the Grand Secretary;

F.

The Grand Master shall at all times have the right of visitation and
inspection of the entire management of this corporation;

G.

The funds of this corporation shall be separately invested under
principles substantially similar to the rules provided in Section 407.040
of this Code; and

H.

The financial statements of this corporation shall be examined by a firm
of independent certified public accountants under principles substantially
similar to the rules provided in Section 407.045 of this Code. Such
audited financial statements shall be submitted to the Committee on
Finance and shall be published in the Proceedings of Grand Lodge.

This Recommendation affects the Boards of the Masonic Homes
of California, the California Masonic Memorial Temple and the California
Masonic Foundation by limiting the term of the presidency of each Board to
five years, the same time limit imposed on the chairmanship of all Grand Lodge
committees. The chairmanship of committees changes on a regular basis, just as
the Master of a Lodge, or even the President of the United States changes, so
that fresh eyes may be cast on past practices to see if any improvements could
be made, either for strength or ornament. There is nothing inherently unique
about a Constitutional Board that would suggest periodic replacement of the
president would be harmful or that bringing fresh leadership would not be a
good thing.
This Recommendation is consistent with the policy and general
purposes of this Grand Lodge.

Grand Master Cooper’s Recommendation No. 2
Names Legislative Analysis Committee

For many years the Committee on Policy and General Purposes has
served Grand Lodge well by explaining the meaning and impact of proposed
legislation at the Annual Communication. As originally envisioned, the committee
was designed to explain to the delegates whether a proposed piece of legislation
was consistent with the purposes of Freemasonry in general, or of our Grand
Lodge in particular. That meant that if a proposal had little or nothing to do with
Freemasonry, or with the proper subject of the governance of our Grand Lodge,
the committee could and would point it out to the voting delegates. In addition,
the committee was expected to make a similar statement as to whether a particular
proposal was consistent with the policy of our Grand Lodge as understood by
the committee.
Over time it has become apparent that the major task of the committee
is to explain proposed legislation to the voting delegates in a clear and concise
manner, to offer a legislative history of the development of a proposal, and to give
the voting delegates an idea as to any concerns that the proposed legislation will
raise for Grand Lodge. It has also become more and more difficult to determine
whether there is a “policy” of Grand Lodge which is separate from that which
is currently expressed in the California Masonic Code, or contained in our
adopted ritual.
In light of the above, it is my recommendation that the name of the
Policy and General Purposes Committee be changed to the Legislative Analysis
Committee. The duties of the committee would be modified also. These changes
will make it clearer as to the responsibilities of the committee to our Grand Lodge,
and still permit them to explain how a particular proposal fits within the overall
framework of the purpose of Freemasonry or of our Grand Lodge, and, if the
circumstances warrant, how the proposal may affect how our law is currently
interpreted and implemented.
If you adopt this recommendation, the following changes will be made
to the Code. Section 406.065 of the Code would be amended to read as marked:
§406.065. LEGISLATIVE
PURPOSES.

ANALYSIS

POLICY

AND

GENERAL

The Committee on Legislative Analysis Policy and General Purposes shall consist
of not less than five nor more than nine members. It shall explain to the members
of Grand Lodge in a clear and concise manner any matter referred to it, offer a
legislative history of the development of a proposal, explain any concerns that the
matter may raise for Grand Lodge and how it fits within the overall framework
of the purpose of Freemasonry or of the Grand Lodge and, if the circumstances

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

175

warrant, explain how the proposal may affect how the law is currently interpreted
and implemented consider and report on matters referred to it as to whether any
action taken or proposed is consistent with the general purposes and policies of
Grand Lodge.
In addition, Sections 403.045 and 406.005 of the Code would be
amended to substitute the words ‘Legislative Analysis’ for the words ‘Policy and
General Purposes.’
Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
In this recommendation, the Grand Master is proposing to change
the name of the Policy and General Purposes Committee to the Committee
on Legislative Analysis and to more precisely define the responsibilities of
that committee. Specifically, this resolution changes Section 406.605 of the
California Masonic Code from a statement that the committee is to consider
and report on whether any particular piece of legislation is consistent with
our policies and general purposes to a directive to explain any matter referred
to it, provide a legislative history, explain concerns that the legislation raises,
describe how that legislation fits within the framework of Freemasonry in
general and/or of Grand Lodge specifically, and explain how the proposal would
affect our current practices. This recommendation, if passed, will not change
what this committee already does when it considers each piece of legislation
at every Annual Communication, but the changes would lead to a more formal
documentation of those considerations and a longer report.
Many years ago, this committee made formal recommendations
regarding how the members should vote, and at times, the recommendations
led to heated debates. For this reason, the current practice of the committee has
been simply to conclude each report with a judgment regarding the consistency
of the legislation. Should this recommendation become law, there will no longer
be any requirement for the committee to classify legislation as being consistent
or not consistent.
Since the committee will continue to make the same considerations of
legislation as it currently is doing, this Recommendation is consistent with the
policy and general purposes of this Grand Lodge.
Recommendation APPROVED.

Grand Master Cooper’s Recommendation No. 3
Allows Research Lodges to Call Up and Down at Meetings

Research lodges perform a unique function in our Grand Lodge. They
provide Masonic education for their members and visitors, as well as developing
programs on Masonic education for other lodges when requested to do so. They
hold quarterly stated meetings, rather than monthly stated meetings, and these
quarterly meetings are often the occasion for the presentation of papers. Under our
current law, a lodge meets in the Entered Apprentice Degree for its stated meeting.
It may call up to receive a candidate proficiency, but not for any other purpose.
Research lodges do not have candidates, and so this provision does not apply to
them. But research lodges do present papers which may, on occasion, only be
suitable for the presence of Fellow Craft Masons or Master Masons. Under our
current law the research lodge cannot receive such papers on their stated meeting
nights because there is no provision for them to meet in a lodge of Fellow Craft
Masons or Master Masons.
This recommendation would allow a research lodge to call up to the
Fellow Craft Degree or to the Master Mason Degree at any meeting in order
to receive a paper appropriate to that degree. This will give research lodges the
flexibility that they need to discharge their proper function as a research lodge,
and to be of greater service to Freemasonry.
If you adopt this recommendation, Section 814.000 of the Code would
be amended to read as marked:
§814.000. RESEARCH LODGES.

to conduct research, hold discussions, gather and preserve Masonic information,

conduct a program of general service to the Craft in the field of Masonic education
and information. Research Lodges shall be subject to all provisions of this Code
applicable to Constituent Lodges, except as follows:

Grand Master Cooper’s Recommendation No. 4
Permits Bunco as a Lodge Activity
Bunco is universally played as a recreational game and is not considered
to be a form of gambling. Much like the recreational playing of bingo, Bunco
should be available for recreational use by our lodges, hall associations, the
concordant and appendant bodies, and our Masonic youth organizations. As long
as the game is recreational in nature, with no gambling involved, there is no reason
that Bunco should not be a permitted activity. It is therefore my recommendation
that the California Masonic Code be changed to reflect this.
If you adopt this recommendation, the following changes will be made
to the Code. Section 811.050 of the Code would be amended to read as marked:
§811.050. BINGO AND BUNCO.
A Lodge may sponsor a bingo or Bunco game, if the Lodge observes the
following rules:
A.

Attendance at the event is limited to the sponsor’s members, their
families and friends;

B.

There are no signs or other advertising visible to the general public
referring to the game;

C.

No donation, admission fee, meal purchase or other charge is accepted or
required for the opportunity to participate; and

D.

Prizes of minimal value may be awarded if purchased by the sponsor
or donated.

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
As it is played today, bunco is a social dice game. According to a 2007
article in the Washington Post, in bunco, “Players take turns rolling three dice
in a series of rounds. In the first round, they get points if they roll ones. In the
second round, they get points if they roll twos, and so on. If they roll three-ofa-kind in the same numbered round -- for example, three fours in round four-that’s bunco, and they get extra points. There is no strategy or decision-making
required, only luck at rolling the dice. The person with the most points at the

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

181

end of the night [is the winner].” Masonic Organizations are currently permitted
to sponsor bingo games so long as certain rules are followed. These same rules
would apply to any Masonically-affiliated bunco game. Given the similarities
between bingo and bunco regarding the importance of luck, there would appear
to be no Grand Lodge policy that should prohibit a Masonic Organization from
sponsoring a bunco game.
This Recommendation is consistent with the policy and general
purposes of this Grand Lodge.
Recommendation APPROVED.
Grand Master Cooper’s Recommendation No. 5
Modifies Automatic Expulsion Procedures
Under our law, a Mason who pleads guilty or no contest to, or is convicted
of, a crime involving moral turpitude is automatically expelled from the fraternity.
Our current law defers the effective date of the expulsion until the accused has
exhausted his appeal rights after his trial. However, the Mason remains in the
craft only if the appeal court reverses his conviction for the reason that he did not
commit the offense. The chairs of our Jurisprudence and Trial Review Committees
know of no instance when there has been such a reversal. This deferral right places
an undue burden on the Grand Lodge staff and committees, because it is difficult
sometimes to determine whether the convicted Mason still has appeal rights. The
chairs of our Jurisprudence and Trial Review Committees have therefore asked
that this deferral be eliminated, and the adoption of this recommendation would
effect that repeal. If you adopt this recommendation, a Mason would be expelled
on his conviction but would be reinstated in the unlikely event that his conviction
is later reversed for the reason that he did not commit the offense.
If you adopt this recommendation, Section 1404.820 of the Code would
be amended to read as marked to make this change:
§1404.820. CONVICTION OF A CRIME OF MORAL TURPITUDE.
A.

If a Mason under the disciplinary jurisdiction of this Grand Lodge
has pleaded guilty or nolo contendere (or no contest) to, or has been
convicted of, a crime of moral turpitude by a federal or state court, he
shall be deemed automatically expelled from all the rights and privileges
of Masonry without any further action of his Lodge or Grand Lodge.
His expulsion shall be effective when he enters his plea of guilty or nolo
contendere (or no contest) or, if he is convicted after entering a plea of
not guilty, at the time of his conviction when the time for appeal of his
conviction has lapsed or the judgment of conviction has been affirmed

182

Proceedings of the
on appeal. Expulsion is automatic, irrespective of an order granting
probation following such conviction, suspending the imposition of
penalty, or of a subsequent order allowing such person to withdraw his
plea of guilty and to enter a plea of not guilty, or setting aside the plea
or verdict of guilty, or dismissing the accusation or information, unless,
for the reason that he did not commit the offense, he either has been
pardoned or has had his judgment of conviction vacated or reversed.

B.

Upon learning that a Mason under the disciplinary jurisdiction of this
Grand Lodge has pleaded guilty or nolo contendere (or no contest) to,
or has been convicted of, a crime of moral turpitude by a federal or state
court, the Grand Secretary shall procure a certified copy of the record
of conviction and provide a copy to the Committee on Jurisprudence.
If in the judgment of a majority of the members of the Committee on
Jurisprudence the Mason has pleaded guilty or nolo contendere (or no
contest) to, or has been convicted of, a crime of moral turpitude by a
federal or state court, then, once the resulting expulsion is effective, the
Grand Secretary shall notify the Mason by certified mail, return receipt
requested, postage prepaid, addressed to his last known address as shown
in the Grand Lodge’s records, of his expulsion from his Lodge or Lodges
in this Jurisdiction. The notification shall include an explanation of his
status as an expelled Mason.

C.

The Grand Secretary shall also notify the Mason’s Lodge of his
expulsion. If the Mason is a member of more than one Lodge, the
notification shall be given to every Lodge of which the Mason is a
member, as shown in Grand Lodge’s records. At the next Stated Meeting
of each Constituent Lodge receiving the Grand Secretary’s notification,
the Master shall announce the Mason’s expulsion. The Master shall
admonish the members present that the name of the expelled Mason, his
criminal record and his expulsion may not be disclosed, either directly or
indirectly, to any person not otherwise entitled to the same. The Secretary
shall record in the minutes of the meeting the particulars of the Grand
Secretary’s notification.

D.

Grand Lodge shall have original jurisdiction to resolve any disputes
under this section.

E.

Nothing contained in this section shall prohibit a Mason from being
tried for the actual conduct upon which criminal charges have been
filed against him or his criminal conviction was based, regardless of the
pendency of any appeal.

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

183

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
Currently there is a major anomaly in the provisions of our Code
dealing with automatic expulsions. Under our current law, if a Mason pleads
guilty or no contest to a crime involving moral turpitude he is automatically
and immediately expelled from our Fraternity. However, if that same Mason
has been convicted by a judge or jury having heard the actual evidence against
him, that Mason cannot be automatically expelled if he has filed an appeal of
his conviction.
It is the policy of this Grand Lodge to treat all Masons equally. There
is no compelling reason to treat a Mason who has admitted his crime differently,
meaning more harshly, than one who has been found guilty by his peers but is
appealing his conviction.
This Recommendation is consistent with the policy and general
purposes of this Grand Lodge.
Report of the Committee on Trial Review:
Our Code currently provides that any Brother convicted of a crime of
moral turpitude is expelled from Masonry effective on the date of his conviction.
It also provides that if the period of time to appeal the conviction has not yet run or
if the conviction is up on appeal the expulsion is delayed until the appeal is over.
The provision which provides for a suspension of the expulsion while
the appellate period is active has been problematic and in the Committee’s
opinion unnecessary. Criminal convictions in California are final when rendered.
An appeal does not stay the effect. Our current Code is therefore not consistent
with California law. In addition, the Code currently provides that as Brother’s
expulsion may be set aside if an appellate court reverses his conviction because
it determines he is factually innocent. That has not happened once during the
effective dates of the automatic expulsion provision. The reason for that is that it
is extremely rare for an appellate court to reverse because of innocence. And if
that did occur, then Grand Master would then simply order the brother reinstated.
There are also additional problems with the current code. First, appeals
generally take between 12 and 36 months to process. This leads to the anomalous
situation in which a brother who is a convicted criminal can attend lodge meetings
and social events as a full-fledged member until his appeal is exhausted. And
second, it can be very difficult to determine whether or not a case is up on appeal
and therefore we have had instances in which brothers have been expelled while
their appeals have still been pending in an unintentional violation of our Code. We

184

Proceedings of the

have also had one brother convicted of murder and sentenced to death. A death
penalty appeal takes 20 - 30 years to process and, while he certainly will not be
visiting any lodges during that period, he would remain a Master Mason with all
the rights and privileges pertaining thereto while he sits on death row. That is a
situation we cannot tolerate.
Grand Master’s Decision No. 5 seeks to solve all of these problems. As
such, the Committee on Trial review strongly supports a Yes vote.
Recommendation APPROVED.
Grand Master Cooper’s Recommendation No. 6
Revokes the Charter of Sublime-Benicia Lodge No. 5
The charter of Sublime-Benicia Lodge No. 5 was originally
suspended by Grand Master Frank Loui on December 2, 2011. The reasons listed
in the letter of suspension were:
• Administrative and financial problems; and
• The use of violence and hazing in the conferral of degrees.
The suspension of the charter was continued by Grand Master John
Lowe, and in a letter of February 7, 2013 to the lodge he indicated that these
problems had not been seriously addressed by the lodge. In addition, he noted that
the lodge was “in disharmony and disarray.” He gave them until August 15 of that
year to produce a plan that would correct these deficiencies. The lodge failed to do
so. On October 7, 2013, I continued the suspension of the lodge, and on October
11, 2013, I personally visited the lodge to discuss what needed to be done to bring
about the return of their charter. There was no response to the conditions that
I set forth.
In November, 2013, I appointed Past Grand Master Richard Wakefield
Hopper to conduct an independent investigation of the situation at SublimeBenicia Lodge No. 5. On March 24, 2014, I received a report from him on the
results of his thorough and exhaustive investigation into the problems afflicting
the lodge. The following statement was made in that report:
It is my opinion based on my investigation that the brethren of Sublime
Benicia Lodge No. 5 are not willing to listen, but would rather speak and
push their own agenda.
On June 28, 2014, I again personally met with the members of the lodge.
At that meeting I informed them that I would present charges against the lodge
pursuant to Section 813.020 of the California Masonic Code in writing at their
stated meeting of August 1, 2014. I did so, and the charges included a continuing

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

185

inability to address the serious financial and administrative deficiencies in the
lodge, and a failure to address the divisiveness and disharmony which was all
too evident at every meeting. I gave them until September 15, 2014, to respond
in writing to these charges. The response I received on September 5, 2014, were
not materially different than the previous responses given to Grand Lodge over
the past several years while the charter has been suspended. The response failed
utterly to address in a serious manner the gravity of the charges, and to provide a
plan to correct the violations of the California Masonic Code and the disharmony
which infects the lodge.
On September 29, 2014, I once more met with the lodge in person to
inform them that my investigation of the lodge, and their response to the charges
delivered to them on August 1, had left me with no other choice that to recommend
to Grand Lodge that the charter be revoked. Accordingly, I recommend that Grand
Lodge revoke the charter of Sublime-Benicia Lodge No. 5, and that the assets
of the lodge be held “in trust” by Grand Lodge for the Masonic community in
Benicia, which may include the eventual chartering of one or more lodges there.
Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The charter of Sublime-Benicia Lodge No. 5 was suspended in
December 2011 by Most Worshipful Frank Loui because of administrative
and financial irregularities and the use of violence and hazing in the conferral
of the degrees. Grand Masters Lowe and Cooper continued the suspension
and attempted to work with Lodge members to resolve these problems, but
without success.
Section 813.040 of the California Masonic Code states that a Lodge’s
charter may be revoked by Grand Lodge for “the neglect or violation of any
duty imposed upon a Lodge in its Charter or in this Code.”
This Recommendation is consistent with the policy and general
purposes of this Grand Lodge.
Recommendation APPROVED.

Permits The Officers Coach to Use the Cipher in a Tiled Meeting

The proponents of this Resolution seek to permit the Officers Coach to use the
approved cipher ritual in a tiled meeting.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, a qualified officers coach is essential to the proper
instruction and delivery of our ritual work in our lodges, and
WHEREAS, the ritual cipher of this jurisdiction is widely used and
referred to during independent and lodge instructional practices, and
WHEREAS, we should be striving for ritual quality and consistency.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Section 402.030 of
the California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§402.030. CIPHER RITUALS.
Grand Lodge shall cause to be prepared, published and sold to Constituent Lodges
and Master Masons, for use and possession by Master Masons only, a cipher
of the esoteric or secret portion of the Ritual, in any medium capable of being
rendered into clearly legible tangible form, as shall be approved from time to time
by the Grand Lecturer with the approval of the Grand Master. The cipher may
include such attached or separate supplements as shall be approved from time to
time by the Grand Lecturer with the approval of the Grand Master. The foregoing
notwithstanding, a Master Mason who is an authorized Candidate’s Coach may
reproduce that portion of the approved cipher ritual that pertains to the Entered
Apprentice and Fellow Craft proficiency examinations for use and possession by
an Entered Apprentice or Fellow Craft to prepare for his proficiency examination.
In no event shall any cipher ritual, or portion thereof, be used during a tiled
meeting, except as follows:
A.

A cipher ritual may be used at any tiled meeting by the duly appointed
Officers’ Coach of the Lodge, or in his absence, a qualified Past Master
selected by the Master; and

B.

A cipher ritual may also be used at any tiled where such meeting is called
for the purpose of practicing the Ritual., Such use, however, shall be
permitted only by members any Mason who are is not participating in the
presentation of the Ritual.

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

187

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of this resolution seek to allow the Officers’ Coach of
a Lodge to use the California Cipher Ritual during a tiled meeting.
In the years since this Grand Lodge approved and began using the
California Cipher Ritual , it has been the rule that the Cipher not be used in a
tiled meeting unless that meeting was called for a practice of the Ritual.
Time has shown that in some cases this practice has not had the
preferred results. Ritual poorly performed in tiled meetings, whether stated or
degree has often resulted in embarrassment to the officers and candidates. Poor
quality of ritual during degrees may also leave the Candidate questioning his
decision to become a Mason.
Although the Officers’ Coach is permitted to give prompts, he himself
may have drawn a blank, and his use of the Cipher during a tiled meeting
would aid him to insure the Ritual is properly performed.
Arguments have been made that a good Officers’ Coach should not
need to use the Cipher, as he should be perfect in all the Ritual. While this
argument is laudable, it is not possible in all Lodges. Most Lodges find it
extremely difficult to have someone to serve as an Officers’ Coach who is a
perfect ritualist.
The Officers’ Coach is an important part of the ritual team in our
jurisdiction. It is necessary therefore to give him all the tools possible to fulfill
his task.
However, it should be noted that this resolution does not address the
situation in which the Officers’ Coach is also participating in the Ritual.
This resolution is consistent with the policy and general purposes of
this Grand Lodge.
Report of the Committee on Ritual:
This resolution seeks to allow the Officers Coach or, in his absence, a
brother appointed by the Master, the OPTION of using a cipher during tiled lodge
meetings and degrees. The key word here is “OPTION”.
In evaluating the merits of this resolution we asked ourselves why it
would be necessary for the fraternity to take a step backward from an expectation
of total ritual excellence to allow the OPTIONAL use of a cipher by an
officer’s coach.
It is expected that our ritual is to be delivered and coached from memory.
Yet, we can all remember lectures were the delivering brother, at several points,
lost his confidence or mental outline. We can also recall times when the officer’s
coach also lost his concentration and was unable to assist in a timely manner. Either
of these situations can cause a less than desirable experience for the candidate.

188

Proceedings of the

Recent instruction by our Grand Lodge leadership teaches us that all
lodges will go through a life cycle from birth, to growth, to maturity, to decline,
and to death or renewal. As members of this fraternity it is our duty to be aware of
those lodges that are in the later life stages and when necessary provide assistance
to lodges that are in the decline and/or rebuilding stages in order to ensure their
future success.
Fortunately, most lodges have developed a culture of ritual excellence
that will postpone the inevitable timeline, however, there will always be some
lodges whose developing ritual culture, especially related to the delivery of the
lectures, although minimally acceptable, is still in some form of distress and
whose members and coaches are in search of assistance.
I then recalled an instruction given to me in a preceding degree where
we were taught that, “To relieve the distressed is a duty incumbent on all men, but
particularly on Masons”.
The spirit of that admonition should guide your decision as Masons in
the treatment of other Masons in this matter. Whereas your lodge may be at the
pinnacle of their life cycle and not require the application of this option, other
lodges in the later life cycles, may not be so lucky.
This resolution should be viewed as your effort to relieve the distress of
other Masons who, while in the declining or rebuilding stages of their lodge’s life
cycle, struggle to improve their ritual. Adoption of this resolution is tantamount to
your stretching forth a helping hand to that lodge by empowering the Master with
an OPTION to allow a newly developing officer’s coach (or a temporary brother)
the ability to follow along in the Cipher during a tiled meeting (particularly degree
lectures) thereby contributing to (1) a quality experience for the candidate, (2) the
eventual improvement in the delivery of the ritual, and (3) the improvement in
the lodge’s life cycle to a point where reliance on the Cipher becomes obsolete.
The Ritual Committee encourages your support of this resolution.
Resolution ADOPTED.

Resolution No. 13-09
Requires the Warden Columns to Remain in Place
While Lodge is Free From Restraint
The proponents of this Resolution seek to change the Ritual to allow the Wardens’
columns are to remain in the position indicating the lodge is at labor while it is
free from restraint.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, the changing of the columns originated in the 18th century
when the lodge ate and drank at the table while conferring the work (before there
were purpose-built lodge rooms); and
WHEREAS, the columns were the signal to the brethren that they were
either “at labor” (and under the direction of the Senior Warden), or at “refreshment”
(and under the direction of the Junior Warden); and
WHEREAS, in ancient California Masonry, when the Master declared
the lodge “free from restraint,” the Wardens’ columns remained in the position to
indicate the lodge was still technically at labor; and
WHEREAS, between 1991 and 2001, the Ritual was amended to require
the Wardens’ columns to be in the position to indicate the lodge was at refreshment
while it was free from restraint as a reminder to all present that although the lodge
was still at labor some restraints have been temporarily lifted; and
WHEREAS, while free from restraint, there exists a conflict between
the altar jewels which indicate the lodge is at “Labor” and the Wardens’ columns
being in a position to indicate the lodge is at “Refreshment;” and
WHEREAS, free from restraint is defined as a time when the Master
desires to give a break in ordinary routine of the Lodge, when the business of the
Lodge is interrupted for a short conference or the setting up of paraphernalia; and
WHEREAS, while free from restraint the brethren do not leave the
room without the Master’s permission but can talk quietly to a neighbor on the
sidelines; and
WHEREAS, while the columns are as currently situated, some brethren
have become confused and believe they can wander about the lodge, and go in and
out of the lodge without the Master’s permission; and
WHEREAS, evidence supports the fact that the Wardens’ columns
should be in either of two positions depending on lodge activity: (1) to indicate
when it is at “labor” and (2) to indicate when it is at “refreshment;” and

190

Proceedings of the

WHEREAS, evidence supports the fact that even though the Master
declares the lodge free from restraint, the Master remains in charge of the Lodge,
the altar jewels remain unchanged, the members do not walk between the altar and
the East, and alarms continue to be given, consequently, the lodge is, technically,
still at labor.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Ritual be amended
to provide that the Wardens’ columns to remain in the position indicating the
lodge is at LABOR when the Master calls it to be FREE FROM RESTRAINT.
Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of this Resolution seek to change our ritual by having
the Senior Warden keep his column up when a Lodge is declared “free from
restraint” instead of laying his column down and the Junior Warden raising his
column . In our jurisdiction, we sign to the East regardless of whose charge the
Lodge is in.
When a Lodge is “free from restraint,” technically it remains at labor.
A Brother entering a Lodge room while it is “free from restraint” must conduct
himself in the same manner as when the Lodge is at labor. Any confusion a
Brother has as to how to act while the Lodge is “free from restraint” and
not “at refreshment” would not be solved by changing the position of the
columns. Rather, the Brother should be given instruction regarding the
distinction between “free from restraint” and “at refreshment” and taught to
act accordingly. It is not the policy of this Grand Lodge to make changes to
ritual without a strong reason to do so.
This Resolution is not consistent with the policy and general purposes
of this Grand Lodge.
Report of the Committee on Ritual:
The proponents of this resolution seek a change in our ritual by
discontinuing the practice of changing the Wardens’ columns when the Master
calls the lodge to be “free from restraint”.
The Grand Lecturer is charged with being the custodian of the ritual as
it has been handed down from our past ritual custodians. While some may have
been taught differently in the past, conversations with our Past Grand Lecturers
determined that in California the ritual has always been to change the Wardens’
columns and, by leaving the altar jewels unchanged, remind the Brethren of the
current status of the lodge, that of being “free from restraint.”
Although the practice in other jurisdictions may be to keep the Wardens’
columns in a position to indicate labor while free from restraint, California’s ritual
evolved to move the columns while leaving the altar jewels unchanged.

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

191

Today’s ritual is a time honored, tested and proven tradition of instruction
that should not be changed. In fact, a recent survey of our Craft made it very clear
that you wanted ritual changes to stop. Consequently, it is the policy of the Ritual
Committee to not recommend changes to our ritual that have not proven over the
years to be a burden to the Fraternity in general or to a lodge in particular.
The current ritual in California of changing the columns while free
from restraint should continue and the Ritual Committee does not support
this resolution.
Resolution NOT ADOPTED.
Resolution No. 13-11
Creates Guidelines for Life Membership Installment Payments
The proponents of this Resolution seek to allow, and establish rules for, the
purchase of a life membership on an installment basis.
[Note: This legislation has been modified because of the adoption of Resolutions
12-04, 12-07 and 13-13.]
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, the existence of a life membership program in a Lodge and
the participation in it by its members is a contributor to the long-term financial
stability of the Lodge; and
WHEREAS, the inability of many members to afford a life
membership often precludes a Lodge from having income far into the
future; and
WHEREAS, a purchaser of a life membership in installments
would receive a contract guaranteeing his rights and responsibilities for the
purchase; and
WHEREAS, a purchaser of a life membership in installments would be
assured of its purchase price once he commences, even though dues thereafter are
increased; and
WHEREAS, if for any reason the purchase is not completed within the
required period of time, the money paid by the member would be refunded; and
WHEREAS, an installment account would provide a source to pay dues,
if a purchaser thereof became liable to being suspended for non-payment of dues,
and he consented thereto; and

192

Proceedings of the

WHEREAS, all funds received for an installment purchase of a life
membership would be kept separate from all other Lodge funds until the purchase
has been completed; and
WHEREAS, all funds would be returned to a member’s family
if he were to die before completing the installment purchase of his life
membership; and
WHEREAS, no Lodge should keep installment payments for any
member whose dues are remitted.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Section 809.150 of
the California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§809.150. LIFE MEMBERSHIP FUND.
A.

All amounts paid for a life membership shall constitute a permanent Life
Membership Fund, which shall be segregated into one or more accounts
which are separate from all other Lodge funds, investments and assets.

B.

A Lodge may only invest its Life Membership Fund as provided in
Section 809.130 of this Code.
Funds received for the purchase of life memberships under an installment
purchase and payment option shall be held in a segregated account which
may only be invested in cash, savings accounts or certificates of deposit.
Such funds may not be deposited into a Lodge’s Life Membership Fund,
nor may they be deposited into a Lodge’s general fund or other multipurpose account. Any fees associated with such segregated account shall
be borne by the Lodge and not by any other source. The total sum paid
into such segregated account together with the income thereon shall
be released from such account only as provided in Section 809.325 of
this Code.
A Lodge’s Life Membership Fund may not be used to secure or fund any
loan to a Lodge or Hall Association, nor may it be used as collateral for a
mortgage or promissory note to or for the benefit of any entity or person.

C.

A Lodge may make withdrawals from its Life Membership Fund for the
general use of the Lodge in the following manner only:
1.

The December 31st value of the Lodge’s Life Membership Fund
for each of the prior three years shall be averaged together. The
maximum allowable withdrawal during the calendar year shall
be 4.0% of that averaged value, except as follows:

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

193

a.

If the Life Membership Fund of a Lodge has existed
for less than three complete calendar years, but for at
least one complete calendar year, the December 31st
value for each year in which the Fund was in existence
shall be averaged together. The maximum allowable
withdrawal during the calendar year shall be 4.0% of
that averaged value; and

b.

If the Life Membership Fund of a Lodge was created
in the prior calendar year, the maximum allowable
withdrawal during the calendar year shall be 4.0%
of the value on December 31st of the prior calendar
year; and

c.

If the Life Membership Fund of a Lodge was created
during the current calendar year, no withdrawals may
be made during the calendar year;

2.

Lodge withdrawals from its Life Membership Fund during each
calendar year may be made in one or more increments, provided
that the total withdrawal for the calendar year does not exceed
the maximum allowable withdrawal as calculated in paragraph
1 above. If a Lodge fails to withdraw any or all of the amount to
which it would have otherwise been entitled during a calendar
year, then it shall be prohibited from taking that withdrawal in
any subsequent year; and

3.

Permissible withdrawals under this section shall be transferred
to the Lodge’s bank or other investment accounts for the general
use of the Lodge.

The Grand Secretary shall provide the Lodges with a form which may be
used to make the calculations described above.
No Lodge is obligated to take withdrawals from its Life
Membership Fund.
D.

A Lodge may, at its option, retain the Grand Lodge to manage the
investment and administration of its Life Membership Fund on behalf of
the Lodge. Such action may be taken at any Stated Meeting by a two thirds
vote of the members present. Such proposed action must be presented, in
writing, at a preceding Stated Meeting and written notice must be given
to each Lodge member setting forth the text of the proposed action and
the date of the Stated Meeting at which the vote is to be taken. It shall
have no effect until approved by the Grand Master. The Secretary of the
Lodge shall note in the minutes of the Lodge the notice of the proposed
action when made. When transmitting the action for approval, he shall
forward a certificate, under seal, showing that the law has been complied
with and that the action has received the required vote.

194

Proceedings of the
Upon approval by the Grand Master, the Lodge shall transfer its entire
Life Membership Fund, including all principal and then undistributed
income, to the Grand Treasurer, to be placed in a Grand Lodge Life
Membership Trust Fund. The Grand Lodge Life Membership Trust Fund
shall be physically segregated from all other funds, investments and
assets of the Grand Lodge and shall be invested and administered by
the Grand Lodge as provided in this Code for a Lodge Life Membership
Fund. The Grand Treasurer may pool all Lodge Life Membership Funds
under its management as one common fund for investment purposes,
provided that there is a separate accounting and valuation of each
individual participating Lodge’s funds at least semi-annually.
The Grand Lodge shall distribute annually in March to each participating
Lodge for its general use its permissible withdrawal, calculated as of the
last market day of the prior calendar year, from its separate share of the
Grand Lodge Life Membership Trust Fund.
All future payments for life memberships purchased by any member of
a participating Lodge shall be recorded by the Secretary in the Lodge’s
membership and financial records and then immediately transferred to
the Grand Treasurer, to be placed in such Lodge’s separate share of the
Grand Lodge Life Membership Trust Fund. A Lodge participating in the
Grand Lodge Life Membership Trust Fund may not keep or administer a
separate Life Membership Fund.
A Lodge may terminate Grand Lodge’s management of the investment
and administration of its Life Membership Fund by a majority vote of
the members present at a Stated Meeting; and the Secretary shall note
the same in the minutes of the Lodge and forward a certificate, under
seal, notifying the Grand Secretary of this action, whereupon the Grand
Treasurer shall return to the Lodge its full interest in the Grand Lodge
Life Membership Trust Fund.
No Lodge shall be required to participate in a Life Membership Fund
administered by the Grand Lodge.

E.

A Lodge purchasing a life membership for the retiring Master as
provided in Section 809.550.D of this Code must transfer the total
purchase price of the life membership from its general funds to its Life
Membership Fund.

F.

A life membership may be purchased as a memorial at any time for a
Master Mason who, at the time of his death, was a member in good
standing of the Lodge. The purchase price for such life membership shall
be paid in full at the time of purchase and calculated in accordance with
Section 809.320 of this Code and the current life membership plan of

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

195

the Lodge. If a Lodge uses the plan described in Section 809.320.B, the
purchase price shall be calculated by using the age of the member at the
time of his death.
G.

Nothing in this Code shall prevent any person from making voluntary
contributions to the Life Membership Fund.

H.

A Life Membership Fund, once established, may never be dissolved
or combined with general Lodge funds, even if there may be no life
members currently living or if further sales of life memberships have
been discontinued.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Section 809.320 of the California
Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§809.320. LIFE MEMBERSHIP.
A Lodge may adopt a standing resolution providing for a life membership plan,
which shall forever exempt a member making the required payment into the plan
from the payment of dues in the Lodge. The resolution may be adopted, amended
or revoked at any Stated Meeting by a majority vote of the members present.
Any such action must be presented, in writing, at a preceding Stated Meeting and
written notice must be given to each Lodge member setting forth the text of the
proposed action and the date of the Stated Meeting at which the vote is to be taken.
The plan must provide that a life membership shall be granted upon payment of:
A.

A sum of money which is not less than 20.83 times the Lodge’s annual
dues at the time of purchase of the life membership; or

B.

A sum of money equal to the Lodge’s annual dues at the time of purchase
of the life membership multiplied by the factor indicated opposite the
member’s age in the following schedule:
Age 49 and under, 21 times annual dues;
50 to 54 inclusive, 19 times annual dues;
55 to 59 inclusive, 17 times annual dues;
60 to 64 inclusive, 14 times annual dues; and
65 and over, 11 times annual dues.

The resolution shall take effect only upon its approval by the Grand Master.
The Secretary shall send to each life member at his last known address, annually,
a Life Membership Dues Card for the next calendar year.

196

Proceedings of the

A life membership is an executed contract. A life member has no interest in
the Lodge’s Life Membership Fund, except in the case of a rescission of his
life membership with his consent and the consent of the Lodge or as elsewhere
provided in this Code.
Upon the rescission of a life membership with the consent of the Lodge and the
life member, the life member shall be paid an amount in cash equal to the lesser
of the original sum of money paid to purchase his life membership or his share of
the fair market value of the Life Membership Fund at the time of the rescission,
as determined by the Grand Treasurer. In making this determination, the Grand
Treasurer shall compute the interest of each living life member in the Lodge’s Life
Membership Fund and the interest of the Lodge in it, on a just and equitable basis.
The Grand Secretary shall provide the form of contract to be used by the Lodge
when a life membership is purchased (other than as a memorial). Such contract
must be signed by the member for whom the life membership is being purchased,
the Lodge Master and the Lodge Secretary, affixed with the seal of the Lodge. The
original shall be kept as part of the member’s permanent membership record. A
copy of the signed contract shall be provided to the member.
A life member who has been suspended or expelled and who shall thereafter
become restored or elected to membership in a Lodge in which a life membership
was once held shall also be restored as a life member of that Lodge.
A Mason who has his dues remitted by the Lodge may not purchase a life
membership nor enter into a contract to purchase a life membership using
an installment purchase and payment option during such time that his dues
are remitted.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that a new Section 809.325 be added
to the California Masonic Code to read as follows:
§809.325. INSTALLMENT PURCHASE OF A LIFE MEMBERSHIP.
A Lodge may include an installment purchase and payment option in its life
membership plan under the following rules:
A.

The Lodge must authorize the installment purchase and payment option
by a separate standing resolution which may be adopted or revoked at
any Stated Meeting by a two-thirds vote of the members present. Any
such action must be presented, in writing, at a preceding Stated Meeting
and written notice must be given to each Lodge member setting forth the
text of the proposed action and the date of the Stated Meeting at which
the vote is to be taken.

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

197

B.

A Mason electing the installment purchase and payment option shall
execute a contract agreeing to pay a purchase price equal to the lump
sum amount he would have paid for a life membership on the date of
the contract. The purchase price shall not increase or decrease during
the term of the contract even though the Lodge may increase or decrease
its annual dues. The Grand Secretary shall provide a form of contract
for the purchase of a life membership using the installment purchase
and payment option. Once completed, such contract must be signed by
the purchasing Mason, the Lodge Master and the Lodge Secretary, and
affixed with the seal of the Lodge. The original contract, or a digital
copy thereof, shall be kept as part of the purchasing Mason’s permanent
membership record. A copy of the contract, affixed with the seal of the
Lodge, shall be provided to the purchasing Mason.

C.

Any life membership contract using an installment purchase and payment
option must comply with the following:
1.

The contract shall include the name of the purchasing Mason,
the name of the issuing Lodge, the purchase price, the date the
contract is signed, the final payment date (which shall be three
years from the date the purchasing Mason signs the contract)
and such other provisions as the Grand Secretary may provide
in the form of contract;

2.

A first installment payment of at least 10% of the total purchase
price must accompany the contract when delivered by the
purchasing Mason. Subsequent payments on the contract may
be made in any amount and at any time and from time to time,
so long as the total purchase price has been paid in full by the
final payment date;

3.

Payments made on the contract shall be held and managed by
the Lodge as provided in Section 809.150.B of this Code until
released as provided in this section;

4.

The purchasing Mason shall have the option to pay his annual
dues to the Lodge from his prior installment payments on the
purchase price, up to the whole balance thereof;

5.

Upon full payment of the purchase price on or before the final
payment due date, the Lodge shall issue the life membership
as provided in the contract, subject to the purchasing Mason
being in good standing, and all amounts paid under the contract
together with any income thereon shall be transferred from
the segregated account to any account of the Lodge’s Life
Membership Fund;

198

Proceedings of the
6.

If full payment of the purchase price has not been made on or
before the final payment date, the contract shall then be null and
void, and all amounts paid under the contract shall be refunded
to the purchasing Mason or his heirs without vote of the Lodge;

7.

If the purchasing Mason dies or demits, withdraws, is expelled
or is suspended from the Lodge before full payment of the
purchase price has been made, the contract shall then be null
and void, and all amounts paid under the contract shall be
refunded to the purchasing Mason or his heirs without vote of
the Lodge;

8.

If the dues of a purchasing Mason are remitted by the Lodge
before full payment of the purchase price has been made, the
contract shall then be null and void, and all amounts paid under
the contract shall be refunded to the purchasing Mason or his
heirs without vote of the Lodge; and

9.

At the purchasing Mason’s option, his life membership contract
may direct that any amounts otherwise refundable to him
or his heirs on the contract shall be transferred instead from
the segregated account to any account of the Lodge’s Life
Membership Fund.

D.

The Lodge shall keep an accurate record of each Mason’s installment
payments and the dates such installment payments are made, providing
a receipt for funds received to the Mason making payment. An
accounting of such payments shall be available to the purchasing Mason
upon request.

E.

A Mason who purchases a life membership in a Lodge using an installment
purchase and payment option must continue to pay the annual dues of
that Lodge, including any increases in the dues, until he has paid in full
the life membership purchase price. The purchasing Mason must be in
good standing in that Lodge on the date his life membership is issued:
his annual dues must be paid in full for the current year on the date
his life membership is issued. His obligation under his life membership
contract and his obligation to continue to pay Lodge dues until his life
membership is issued are mutually exclusive obligations. The purchasing
Mason shall not be entitled to a refund of any part of his annual dues if
his life membership contract is paid in full before the end of the year for
which his dues have already been paid.

§809.350. RETURN OF DUES.
If a Mason of the Lodge dies, is issued a Demit or discontinues his multiple
membership, the Lodge shall refund to his authorized successor in interest or
to him dues paid in advance of the month when he died or his affiliation with
the Lodge terminated; provided, however, that a Mason issued a Demit or

in advance if he has returned his dues receipt in such Lodge with his request for
a Demit or Certificate of Discontinuance of Multiple Membership. There shall

this Code.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Section 809.360 of the California
Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§809.360. REMISSION OF DUES.
If recommended by the Charity Committee, a Lodge, without giving the name
of the delinquent Masons except to the Secretary, may remit to December 31st
of the current calendar year the accrued dues of those of its Masons who are
unable to pay.
The Charity Committee should review the situation of a Mason whose dues
were remitted by a Lodge the preceding calendar year before the February
Stated Meeting. If, in the opinion of the Charity Committee, the necessity for the
remission of his dues still exists, it shall recommend to the Lodge that the dues
be remitted to December 31st of the current calendar year. A Lodge shall not
remit the dues of any of its Masons, for any stated period, or in advance, except
as herein provided.

purchase price under his life membership contract, if any, the contract shall be null
and void, and all amounts paid under the contract shall be refunded, as provided in
Section 809.325 of this Code.
A Mason who is mentally incompetent to such an extent as to be incapable of
taking care of himself, or a member who is a resident of the Masonic Homes of
California, may be considered as unable to pay dues.

Masonic Code be amended as marked:

200

Proceedings of the

§809.370. SUSPENSION FOR NON-PAYMENT OF DUES.
If a Mason has not paid his dues during a period of 12 months, the Secretary
shall notify him that he will be suspended for non-payment of dues unless at
the Lodge’s next Stated Meeting either his dues have been paid or sickness or
inability to pay is shown as the cause for the failure to pay. The notice shall be
given either by certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, addressed
to his last known address, or by actual service of notice, duly certified by the
Tiler. If all dues due and payable have not been paid by the time of the Lodge’s
next Stated Meeting, he shall be declared suspended by the Master, unless for
special reasons shown the Lodge shall remit his dues or grant him further time for
payment. No worthy brother who is unable to pay his dues shall be suspended for
non-payment of dues.
No Mason who has attained the age of 80 years or who has attained an aggregate
number of years in age and years as a Mason in good standing equaling 120 or
more shall be suspended for non-payment of dues without a written report to the
Lodge from the Member Retention Committee evidencing when and where the
committee interviewed the delinquent Mason, why the delinquent Mason has not
paid his dues and whether the delinquent Mason has the ability to pay his dues.
A copy of this report shall be provided to the Grand Secretary at least thirty days
before the vote may be taken on the suspension.
A Mason at his option may pay his dues from his prior installment payments on
the purchase price under his life membership contract, as provided in Section
809.325 of this Code.
A Mason shall not be expelled from Masonry for non-payment of dues.

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of this Resolution seek to allow Lodges with a life
membership plan to permit members to make payments on an installment
plan over multiple years rather than a single lump sum payment as is the
current requirement.
The proposed life membership installment plan would permit a
member to purchase a life membership in multiple payments over a three year
period. During this time the price of the life membership would not increase,
regardless of any dues increases. The member would still be required to make
dues payments until the full purchase price of the life membership had been
made. The Lodge would be required to keep any partial payments in a separate
fund and track any investment income on a member by member basis . Such
funds could only be invested in cash, savings, or certificates of deposit and
must be readily available for withdrawal.
If the purchasing member fails to pay the required sum in three years,
demits, withdraws, is suspended, expelled, or dies, the Lodge would be required
to refund the payments made along with any accrued interest. The member
could also request the Lodge to pay his current dues from the balance of
his partial payments. Any fees resulting from early liquidation of investments
would be borne by the Lodge.
While this plan might make it easier for a member to purchase a life
membership, it also imposes additional bookkeeping requirements on a Lodge
and complexity to its Life Membership Fund investment strategy.
This Resolution is not consistent with the policy and general purposes
of this Grand Lodge.
Resolution NOT ADOPTED.

Modifies the Payment Structure of Life Membership Plans
The proponents of this Resolution seek to modify the sum of money required by

[Note: This legislation has been modified because of the adoption of

To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, a Lodge currently has two options from which to select the
pricing formula for its life memberships; and

202

Proceedings of the

WHEREAS, the use of a decimal number in the single multiple option
is archaic and confusing; and
WHEREAS, the single multiple option currently appears to limit the
purchase price of a life membership, rather than require a minimum; and
WHEREAS, the current pricing schedule of the age-based option – which
requires an investment return of up to 9% – places unreasonable expectations for
return on investments of the less expensive purchases by older members in order
to replace dues income; and
WHEREAS, the current pricing schedule requires unreasonable
expectations of investment returns in order to replace dues income; and
WHEREAS, the proposed pricing schedule – requiring an investment
return of 5% or less – provides for a more reasonable expectation for return on
investments in order to replace dues income.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Section 809.320 of
the California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§809.320. LIFE MEMBERSHIP.
A Lodge may adopt a standing resolution providing for a life membership plan,
which shall forever exempt a member making the required payment into the plan
from the payment of dues in the Lodge. The resolution may be adopted, amended
or revoked at any Stated Meeting by a majority vote of the members present.
Any such action must be presented, in writing, at a preceding Stated Meeting and
written notice must be given to each Lodge member setting forth the text of the
proposed action and the date of the Stated Meeting at which the vote is to be taken.
The plan must provide that a life membership shall be granted upon payment of:
A.

A sum of money which is not less equal to or greater than 20.83 22
times the Lodge’s annual dues at the time of purchase of the life
membership; or

B.

A sum of money equal to the Lodge’s annual dues at the time of purchase
of the life membership multiplied by the factor indicated opposite the
member’s age in the following schedule:
Age 49 and under, 21 times annual dues;
50 to 54 inclusive, 19 times annual dues;
55 to 59 inclusive, 17 times annual dues;
60 to 64 inclusive, 14 times annual dues; and
65 and over, 11 times annual dues.

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

203

Age 18 to 30 inclusive, 25 times annual dues;
Age 31 to 49 inclusive, 23 times annual dues;
Age 50 to 69 inclusive, 21 times annual dues; and
Age 70 and over, 20 times annual dues.
The resolution shall take effect only upon its approval by the Grand Master.
The Secretary shall send to each life member at his last known address, annually,
a Life Membership Dues Card for the next calendar year.
A life membership is an executed contract. A life member has no interest in
the Lodge’s Life Membership Fund, except in the case of a rescission of his
life membership with his consent and the consent of the Lodge or as elsewhere
provided in this Code.
Upon the rescission of a life membership with the consent of the Lodge and the
life member, the life member shall be paid an amount in cash equal to the lesser
of the original sum of money paid to purchase his life membership or his share of
the fair market value of the Life Membership Fund at the time of the rescission,
as determined by the Grand Treasurer. In making this determination, the Grand
Treasurer shall compute the interest of each living life member in the Lodge’s Life
Membership Fund and the interest of the Lodge in it, on a just and equitable basis.
The Grand Secretary shall provide the form of contract to be used by the Lodge
when a life membership is purchased (other than as a memorial). Such contract
must be signed by the member for whom the life membership is being purchased,
the Lodge Master and the Lodge Secretary, affixed with the seal of the Lodge. The
original shall be kept as part of the member’s permanent membership record. A
copy of the signed contract shall be provided to the member.
A life member who has been suspended or expelled and who shall thereafter
become restored or elected to membership in a Lodge in which a life membership
was once held shall also be restored as a life member of that Lodge.
