Proceedings of the

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of this Resolution seek to modify the current formula
for determining the price paid for a life membership.
A life membership is intended to be a mutually beneficial arrangement
between a member and his Lodge. The member avoids future dues increases,
gains the convenience of never having to pay dues again with the assurance
of never being suspended for non-payment of dues, regardless of his future
financial condition. The Lodge gains a sum of money that can be invested to
produce a revenue stream in perpetuity. It is the goal of the Lodge to invest
this sum to gain a rate of return sufficient to compensate for the loss of future
dues payments.
The fair price of a life membership is a function of life expectancy,
inflation (as reflected in future dues increases), and the expected rate of return
over the member’s lifetime. The current pricing formula was determined
years ago during a period when life expectancy was lower and conservative
investments produced a higher rate of return than today. It is reasonable to
revise the formula to take account of these factors.
The current formula requires that a Lodge achieve a higher rate
of return for life memberships purchased by older members in comparison
to younger members. Consider the example of a 65 year old member who
purchases a life membership. Assuming a life expectancy of 90 and no increase
in dues, the Lodge would need an average rate of return of nine percent over
that period in order to avoid a loss. Under the new formula, the Lodge would
need an average rate of return of about two percent in order to break even. For
an 18 year old life member, the Lodge would need an average rate of return of
five percent under the current formula and four percent under the new formula.
The net effect of the new formula is to require a comparable rate of return on
all life memberships, thus simplifying a Lodge’s investment strategy.
This Resolution is consistent with the policy and general purposes of
this Grand Lodge.
Resolution NOT ADOPTED.
Resolution No. 13-20
Creates Procedures to Authorize Cemetery Interment
The proponents of this Resolution seek to clarify that the Charity Committee of
the Lodge may authorize the use of a Lodge’s cemetery property for the interment
of an eligible Mason or family member.

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

205

To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, is the right of every eligible Mason to a Masonic memorial
service; and
WHEREAS, it is the obligation of a Lodge to bury or inter an eligible
Mason; and
WHEREAS, it is the obligation of a Lodge to pay for the necessary
expenses of burial or interment of a deceased member’s widow and orphans when
financial circumstances require it; and
WHEREAS, a necessary part of burial or interment may require the
utilization of cemetery property; and
WHEREAS, many Lodges own cemetery property; and
WHEREAS, it is sometimes impracticable to wait for a Lodge meeting
to authorize use of Lodge cemetery property; and
WHEREAS, there should be a standard authority or committee outside
of a Lodge meeting to authorize interment in cemetery property owned by the
Lodge; and
WHEREAS, the Charity Committee of the Lodge is charged to act with
discretion in the performance of its duties; and
WHEREAS, it should be within the authority of the Charity Committee
– as an extension of its duties – to authorize the interment of eligible persons in
cemetery property owned by the Lodge.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Section 804.820 of
the California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§804.820. RIGHT TO BURIAL.
It is the right of every Mason, other than a demitted, withdrawn, suspended or
expelled Mason, to a Masonic memorial service or burial interment with Masonic
honors. The foregoing notwithstanding, a demitted Master Mason has the right to
a Masonic memorial service or burial interment with Masonic honors if he dies
within a year after receiving a Demit.
It is the duty of the Lodge to bury inter an eligible Mason of that Lodge, wherever
he may have died, and an eligible Mason of another Lodge in this or any other
Jurisdiction who dies within the vicinity of the Lodge. If such deceased Mason’s
financial circumstances require it, the Lodge shall pay the necessary expenses of
the burial interment, even if the deceased Mason’s Lodge refuses to reimburse
the Lodge for such expenses. The Lodge shall reimburse any other Lodge for
the reasonable expenses incurred by it in suitably burying interring one of its
deceased Masons. No Lodge shall fix in advance the amount to be paid for such
burial interment.

206

Proceedings of the

When financial circumstances require it, it is also the duty of the Lodge to pay all
the necessary expenses of the burial interment for one of its deceased member’s
widow and orphans dependent upon her and to reimburse any other Lodge for the
reasonable expenses incurred by it in suitably burying interring them. No Lodge
shall fix in advance the amount to be paid for such burial interment.
When financial circumstances require the Lodge to pay the necessary expenses of
interment, the Charity Committee may, in its discretion, authorize the interment
of the decedent in any cemetery property owned by the Lodge. Additionally, when
financial circumstances require it, the Charity Committee may, in its discretion,
authorize the interment of the deceased spouse, widow, child, orphan, parent or
sibling of a living or deceased Mason of the Lodge in any cemetery property
owned by the Lodge. The Charity Committee shall provide a written report to
the Secretary of the Lodge to authorize any such interment, signed by a majority
of the members of the Charity Committee, upon receipt of which the Lodge
Secretary shall execute as the agent of the Lodge any documentation required of
the Lodge for the interment.
The Charity Committee shall provide a written report to the Lodge of any and
all of their actions under this section, signed by a majority of the members of the
Charity Committee. Such report shall be presented by the Charity Committee at
the next Stated Meeting of the Lodge and included with the minutes.
A Lodge may, in its discretion, conduct Masonic funeral or memorial services for
a Mason of the Lodge suspended for non-payment of dues, if there is no other
Masonic offense established against him, but it shall not pay the expenses of the
burial interment.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that, should this Resolution 1320 be adopted, the Committee on Jurisprudence be authorized to arrange the
provisions of Section 804.820 of the California Masonic Code by paragraphs and
subparagraphs, with or without headings, lettered and numbered as appropriate,
as and to the extent that the committee shall determine.
Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
Lodges are responsible for interring deceased Masons, their widows
and orphans. The proponents of Resolution 13-20 seek to amend our law so that
Lodges can provide an interment site it already owns, if needed, in a timely
fashion. Specifically, changes to California Masonic Code section 804.820 are
being sought that would explicitly permit a Lodge to provide an interment site
it owns without having to wait until a Stated Meeting to vote to do so. Rather
the Lodge Charity Committee would be charged with assessing the situation
and, if appropriate, allow such an interment to take place with a subsequent
report being made to the Lodge at the next convenient time.

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

207

Resolution 13-20 calls for another substantive change in our law. The
CMC at this time only requires the Lodge to be responsible for the interment of
eligible Masons and their widows and dependent orphans. In other words, spouses
and children would only be eligible for assistance if the Mason predeceased
his wife and if both predeceased the deaths of their dependent children. The
proposed new fourth paragraph of CMC section 804.820 authorizes the Lodge
to provide cemetery property it owns to the deceased spouse or child of a living
Mason as well as to deceased parents or siblings of eligible Masons.
It is the obligation of Masons to accept responsibility for the interment
needs of other Masons, their widows and orphans .
This Resolution is consistent with the policies and general purposes
of this Grand Lodge.
Resolution NOT ADOPTED.
Resolution No. 13-21
Creates Procedures to Authorize Funeral Expenses
The proponents of this Resolution seek to clarify that the Charity Committee of
the Lodge may authorize the payment of funeral expenses of an eligible Mason
or family member.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, our laws currently require the Lodge to suitably bury or
inter an eligible Mason; and
WHEREAS, our laws also currently require the Lodge to suitably bury
or inter the widow or orphans of a Mason when financial circumstances require
it; and
WHEREAS, our laws currently allow the Charity Committee to pay for
the relief of a distressed worthy Mason and the wife, widow or orphan of a Master
Mason; and
WHEREAS, sometimes the expense of suitably burying someone may
be beyond the financial resources of a Mason or the wife, widow or orphan of a
Master Mason; and
WHEREAS, a necessary part of suitably burying someone would
reasonably include the necessary professional services of a funeral home, casket
urn or cremation container, and necessary required cash advance items; and
WHEREAS, it is sometimes impracticable to wait for a Lodge meeting
to authorize such expenditures; and

208

Proceedings of the

WHEREAS, there should be a standard authority or committee outside
of a Lodge meeting to authorize such expenditures; and
WHEREAS, the Charity Committee of the Lodge is charged to act with
discretion in the performance of its duties; and
WHEREAS, it should be within the authority of the Charity Committee
– as an extension of its duties – to authorize the payment of funeral expenses
permitted under our law; and
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Section 804.820 of
the California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§804.820. RIGHT TO BURIAL.
It is the right of every Mason, other than a demitted, withdrawn, suspended or
expelled Mason, to a Masonic memorial service or burial interment with Masonic
honors. The foregoing notwithstanding, a demitted Master Mason has the right to
a Masonic memorial service or burial interment with Masonic honors if he dies
within a year after receiving a Demit.
It is the duty of the Lodge to bury inter an eligible Mason of that Lodge, wherever
he may have died, and an eligible Mason of another Lodge in this or any other
Jurisdiction who dies within the vicinity of the Lodge. If such deceased Mason’s
financial circumstances require it, the Lodge shall pay the necessary expenses of
the burial interment, even if the deceased Mason’s Lodge refuses to reimburse
the Lodge for such expenses. The Lodge shall reimburse any other Lodge for
the reasonable expenses incurred by it in suitably burying interring one of its
deceased Masons. No Lodge shall fix in advance the amount to be paid for such
burial interment.
When financial circumstances require it, it is also the duty of the Lodge to pay all
the necessary expenses of the burial interment for one of its deceased member’s
widow and orphans dependent upon her and to reimburse any other Lodge for the
reasonable expenses incurred by it in suitably burying interring them. No Lodge
shall fix in advance the amount to be paid for such burial interment.
When financial circumstances require the Lodge to pay the necessary expenses
of interment, the Charity Committee may draw upon the funds of the Lodge to
pay only the necessary and required expenses for the interment of the decedent
and then only in such amount as shall be determined appropriate in the discretion
of the Charity Committee. Additionally, when financial circumstances require it,
the Charity Committee may, in its discretion, pay only the necessary and required
expenses for the interment of the deceased spouse, widow, child or orphan of a
living or deceased Master Mason of the Lodge. These necessary and required
interment expenses shall be limited to the basic itemized professional fees of a
funeral home; the casket, urn or cremation container (and grave liner if required);
a grave marker; and any additional necessary and required cash advance items.

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

209

These interment expense payments are exempt from any expenditure limitations
of this Code and any limitations in the standing resolution of the Lodge for
charity expenditures. The Charity Committee shall provide a written report to the
Secretary of the Lodge to authorize any such payments, signed by a majority of the
members of the Charity Committee, upon receipt of which the Lodge Secretary
shall execute as the agent of the Lodge any documentation required of the Lodge
for a funeral and/or interment under these provisions.
The Charity Committee shall provide a written report to the Lodge of any and
all of their actions under this section, signed by a majority of the members of the
Charity Committee. Such report shall be presented by the Charity Committee at
the next Stated Meeting of the Lodge and included with the minutes.
A Lodge may, in its discretion, conduct Masonic funeral or memorial services for
a Mason of the Lodge suspended for non-payment of dues, if there is no other
Masonic offense established against him, but it shall not pay the expenses of the
burial interment.

§806.000. COMMITTEES.
A.

The Master and Wardens shall be a Charity Committee, and shall have

The Master, at the Stated Meeting next succeeding his installation, shall
appoint an Auditing Committee, whose duty it shall be to examine all
accounts presented against the Lodge and the books and records of the

on the Audit Committee.

C.

The Master, at the Stated Meeting next succeeding his installation, shall
appoint a Member Retention Committee to personally, or otherwise,
interview each delinquent member, ascertain the cause, and work closely
with the Master and officers in a continuing effort to effect the retention
of all worthy brothers unable to pay.

D.

The Lodge may have such other committees as the Master or the Lodge
may deem proper to appoint. All committees shall be appointed by the
Master, unless the Lodge provides otherwise.

E.

All reports of committees shall be in writing.

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of Resolution 13-21 seek to clarify that the Charity
Committee of a Lodge may authorize the payment of funeral expenses of an
eligible Mason and/or an eligible family member. The Resolution would add
section 804.820 to the California Masonic Code, Right to Burial, outlining

as well as their widows and orphans.

this Grand Lodge.

Resolution No. 13-23
Exempts Valley Lodge No. 135 from the Requirement of Majority Hall
Association Ownership
The proponents of this Resolution seek to exempt Valley Lodge No. 135 from the
requirement that it own its interest in its Masonic Hall through a corporation in
which it has majority control.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

211

WHEREAS, Valley Lodge No. 135 received its charter from the Grand
Lodge of California, Free and Accepted Masons, in 1860 and Scio Lodge No.
102 was instituted by the Grand Lodge of California, Independent Order of Odd
Fellows, in 1861; and
WHEREAS, the community leaders who owned the real property upon
which the original Lodge Hall was erected were members of both Scio Lodge No
102, I.O.O.F. and Valley Lodge No. 135, F.& A.M., a tradition which continues
to this day; and
WHEREAS, these community leaders directed their heirs to see that the
Lodge Hall property in Linden, California was preserved for the use of the local
fraternal organizations, in perpetuity; and
WHEREAS, over time, many of these fraternal organizations ceased to
exist, leaving only Scio Lodge No 102, I.O.O.F. and Valley Lodge No. 135, F.&
A.M., as the co-owners of the property, which ownership relationship dates back
to 1904; and
WHEREAS, when it became necessary to replace the antiquated Lodge
Hall in the 1950s, our Trustees attempted to obtain controlling interest in the
property, in order that Valley Lodge No. 135 might come into compliance with
the existing statutes of the California Masonic Code; and
WHEREAS, neither of the two Lodges were able to come to an accord
at that time, and our recent efforts to do so have met with no better success; and
WHEREAS, our Grand Secretary, the Very Worshipful Allan Casalou
has informed us that our co-ownership relationship is unique in the State of
California; and
WHEREAS, Section 809.110 of the California Masonic Code stipulates
that “A Lodge must retain control and hold title to all money, property and other
assets of the Lodge …”; and
WHEREAS, Section 809.140, Paragraph A, of the California Masonic
Code further defines and limits Lodge Hall ownership to “… membership or
shares in a Masonic Hall Association wherein a Lodge or Lodges collectively
hold a majority of memberships or shares or a controlling interest by such
investment”; and
WHEREAS, certain Lodges have been granted exemptions from
various California Masonic Code statutes, for reasons of inclement weather, the
use of foreign languages in their Degrees or the use of Holy Writings other than
the Christian Bible; and
WHEREAS, Valley Lodge No. 135, F. & A. M. seeks to preserve a
fraternal relationship that was initiated over 150 years ago and that continues
harmoniously to the present, by “grandfathering” the equal, co-ownership
relationship between Scio Lodge No. 102, I.O.O.F. and Valley Lodge No. 135,
F. & A. M.

212

Proceedings of the

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that, any provision of
the California Masonic Code to the contrary notwithstanding, Valley Lodge No.
135, F.&A.M. may own directly an undivided one-half interest in real property
commonly known as 4971 North Mill Street in Linden, California, together with
Scio Lodge No. 102, I.O.O.F. as the owner of the other undivided one-half interest.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that, during the period of such
ownership, Valley Lodge No. 135, F.&A.M. shall not be required to own such
interest through a corporation.

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
This Resolution would exempt Valley Lodge Number 135 from the
requirement that it own a majority interest in its Masonic Hall and legalize
its current ownership arrangement of sharing control with a non-Masonic
fraternal organization.
Section 809.140 of the California Masonic Code requires that if a
property is owned in whole or part by one or more Lodges then the majority
interest must belong to a Lodge or group of Lodges. A Lodge is prohibited
from sharing equal ownership with a non-Masonic entity.
Such a majority ownership requirement protects both the Lodge and
Grand Lodge by ensuring that the property can only be used in accordance
with the CMC and minimizes disagreement and contention. Allowing a Lodge
to function as a non-majority owner of a property might result in liability
due to the partner’s insolvency or malfeasance.
This Resolution is not consistent with the policy and general purposes
of this Grand Lodge.
Report of the Committee on Masonic Properties:
The proponents of Resolution 13-23 seek to exempt Valley Lodge No.
135 from the requirement that a Masonic lodge or lodges own a majority interest
in its Masonic Hall through a corporation.
It further seeks to allow Valley Lodge No. 135 to directly own equal
shares of its Masonic Hall with Scio Lodge No 102, Independent Order of
Odd Fellows.
The California Masonic Code allows a Masonic lodge to invest funds in
or maintain an investment in memberships or shares in a Masonic Hall Association
wherein a Lodge or Lodges collectively hold a majority interest.
Without majority ownership by Valley Lodge this Committee believes
that this partnership cannot be a Masonic Hall Association and therefore would

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

213

not be subject to the laws of this Grand Lodge. Such an arrangement could put the
Lodge at risk and open up Hall Associations state wide to un-due scrutiny.
As it is currently organized, half of their board is not bound to the
California Masonic Code and therefore could make decisions that contradict
Masonic laws and values. Decisions to sell the property submit a Form 200 or
have the lodge’s Inspector audit the books can be blocked by half of the board.
They have equal interest in the corporation and they are not Masons, so they will
not feel obligated to conform to our laws. Earlier this year, the board of trustees of
this association refused to allow the District Inspector for Valley Lodge to attend
the meeting of the association. This is not acceptable.
As we have seen recently, when the government finds a problem in one
Hall Association, they start looking at others. This is why we require the Uniform
Code of By-Laws, strict inspection and reporting, and conformity to our code. This
not only protects the specific Hall Association, but all Masonic Hall Associations.
When the Grand Lodge amended the by-laws to require majority
ownership by Masonic lodges, all other Hall Associations conformed to the new
regulation. Valley Lodge has not conformed. Other Hall Associations, even those
that were equally owned by a Masonic Lodge and a Masonic organization, made
the necessary changes in ownership to conform to the requirement. The proponents
feel that because equal ownership has been a long-standing situation for their
lodge, it should be allowed to continue. Times change and the law requires new
business relationships. Many of our lodges had long standing agreements of equal
ownership and they have conformed to the new laws.
Some argue that there has been a long-standing agreement between the
Masonic Lodge and the Odd Fellows Lodge to share equally in the ownership of
the hall and that Valley Lodge should be an exception to the rule because of this
long-standing agreement. The fact is that there have been other California Lodges
that also had long-standing agreements with other organizations – Masonic
and non-Masonic, but over the years they have changed these arrangements to
conform to the modern laws. Valley Lodge is just the last to comply with what
is now a long-standing ordinance in the California Masonic Code – an ordinance
that is meant to protect Valley Lodge and all lodges in California.
This Committee cannot find any legitimate reason why this one Lodge
should receive an exemption to a regulation that all other Lodges and Hall
Associations have conformed to. Furthermore, we think it is a risk to the fraternity
to make this exception and there is no compelling reason why this risk should
be taken.
Therefore The Masonic Properties Committee recommends a NO vote
to this resolution.
Resolution NOT ADOPTED.

Resolution No. 13-27
Modifies Minimum Dues

The proponents of this Resolution seek to modify the minimum dues of a Lodge.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, the minimum dues of a Lodge have not been changed since
1948; and
WHEREAS, it is important to retain the value of a Lodge
membership; and
WHEREAS, it is vital that the economic viability of our Lodges be
sustained; and
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Section 809.310 of
the California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§809.310. DUES.
A Lodge’s dues shall be established in its Bylaws. The minimum annual dues shall
be $12, plus the Per Capita sum approved by Grand Lodge at the immediately
preceding Annual Communication, with the total thus determined rounded up to
the next whole dollar. The Lodge Secretary shall issue to each Mason paying his
dues a receipt using, without change, the uniform receipt for dues available from
the Grand Secretary.
Dues shall commence with the first day of the month next following the conferring
of the Entered Apprentice Degree or as provided in Sections 804.740 or 804.750
of this Code for Masons joining the Lodge by affiliation.
If a Lodge increases its dues, the increase shall become effective upon the start of
fiscal year of the Lodge following the Grand Master’s approval of the increase.
Masons of the Lodge who have paid their dues in advance for such fiscal year
must pay the increase.

take effect until January 1, 2017.

The proponents of this Resolution seek to modify the minimum dues
of a Lodge.

Section 809.310 of the California Masonic Code states: “A Lodge’s
dues shall be established in its Bylaws. The minimum annual dues shall
be $12.”
The proponents seek to amend this section to make annual dues no less
than $12 plus per capita rounded up to the next whole dollar.
The expenses of running any Lodge increase annually. Raising the
minimum amount of annual dues will help a Lodge use less of its investment
income to meet these expenses, thereby preserving Lodge assets for future use.
This Resolution is consistent with the policy and general purposes of
this Grand Lodge.
Resolution ADOPTED.

Resolution No. 14-01
Clarifies the Grand Master’s Right to Review a Trial Dismissal
The proponents of this Resolution seek to clarify the Grand Master’s right to
review and reinstate a trial dismissal.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, Section 1404.315 of the California Masonic Code allows
the Committee on Jurisprudence to dismiss charges of unmasonic conduct, if in
the judgment of the Committee all of the facts set forth in the charges, if true,
would not warrant a guilty verdict; and
WHEREAS, this power allows the dismissal of unwarranted charges
without the expense and embarrassment of a trial; and
WHEREAS, it would be helpful to clarify the Grand Master’s power to
review a dismissal.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Section 1404.315 of
the California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§1404.315. REVIEW OF THE CHARGES BY THE COMMITTEE ON
JURISPRUDENCE.
The Committee on Jurisprudence shall review all charges and specifications
received by the Grand Secretary, strike out those portions of any charge which
are not supported by a clear and precise specification of unmasonic conduct and
revise those portions of any charge which are incorrect, ambiguous or insufficient,
based on the specifications. The committee may work with the Accuser during its
review. The committee shall append to the charge or charges a statement setting
forth the portion or portions of Section 1401.010 under which each charge is being
brought and every essential factual element of the unmasonic conduct specified
which must be proven at trial in order for the Accused to be found guilty of that
specification. After its review, the Committee on Jurisprudence shall provide the
Grand Secretary with the charge or charges as they may have been revised by the
committee. The Grand Secretary shall provide the Grand Master with a copy of
the charge or charges as revised by the committee upon receipt.
If in the judgment of the Committee on Jurisprudence all of the facts set forth in any
of the charges and specifications, if true, would not warrant a verdict of unmasonic
conduct, then any such charge shall be dismissed by it and the committee shall
so advise the Grand Secretary. Such a dismissal shall not prevent any subsequent

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

219

filing of a charge with more evidence. The Committee on Jurisprudence shall
prepare a written report on its action and file it with the Grand Secretary. The
Grand Secretary shall provide the Grand Master with a copy upon receipt. The
Grand Secretary shall notify the Accuser and the Accused of the action taken, as
well as the Accused’s Lodge and the Inspector assigned to the Accused’s Lodge. If
the Accused is a member of more than one Lodge, the notification shall be given
to every Lodge of which the Accused is a member, as shown in Grand Lodge’s
records, and the Inspector assigned to each such Lodge. The Grand Master may at
his discretion appoint one or more Master Masons to mediate any dispute giving
rise to the filing of any dismissed charges of unmasonic conduct. Alternatively,
the Grand Master may reinstate the dismissed charges as filed if in his view the
facts set forth in any of the charges and specifications, if true, would warrant a
verdict of unmasonic conduct.
Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
As part of the overall revision of the part of the California Masonic Code
that dealt with Masonic Trials several years ago, the Jurisprudence Committee
was charged with reviewing all of the charges and specifications that were
received by the Grand Secretary. That committee was empowered to dismiss
any charge or specification which, even if true, would not warrant a verdict of
unmasonic conduct. While the Grand Master has, by implication, the power
toreinstate the dismissed charges, if, in his opinion, a verdict of unmasonic
conduct would be warranted, this was not stated in section 1404.315. This
resolution adds an explicit sentence to that section stating that fact.
This resolution is consistent with the policy and general purposes of
this Grand Lodge.
Report of the Committee on Trial Review:
Resolution 14-01 seeks to clarify the Grand Master’s power to reinstate
Masonic charges dismissed by the Jurisprudence Committee.
The current procedure is that when charges are filed against a Mason
they are initially sent to the Jurisprudence Committee which reviews the form
of the charges and makes a determination of whether or not they state a Masonic
offense, more specifically they determine that if all of the facts alleged in the
charges are true whether or not they would constitute a Masonic offense. This
process is integral to our purpose because it allows for the weeding out of frivolous
charges and charges which can never result in a conviction, thus saving the grand
lodge and the constituent lodges substantial time and money, and saving those
involved the embarrassment and humiliation of having to go through a trial which
is destined to lead nowhere.

220

Proceedings of the

The Code already requires that when Jurisprudence determines that
charges should be dismissed it shall notify the Grand Secretary and prepare a
report as to the reasons for the dismissal and that that report shall be forwarded to
the Grand Master. CMC §404.130(a) gives the Grand Master general supervisory
power over Grand Lodge during its recess. It can be argued that that power
includes the power to reverse dismissals ordered by the Jurisprudence Committee.
This resolution seeks to clarify that and to specifically establish that
the Grand Master does have the power to reinstate charges after dismissal by
Jurisprudence. It therefore only seeks to clarify that the Grand Master has that
power. It does not give him the power to reverse a decision of Grand Lodge. If the
case is reinstated it will proceed to trial and the result will ultimately be reviewed
by the Committee on Trial Review and voted on by Grand Lodge. This resolution
does not change that.
While it is true that not all Grand Masters are lawyers the function of
the Jurisprudence Committee is designed to guide the Grand Master on the legal
complexities involved in a particular case. Additionally, our law provides that
the Grand Master shall have the ultimate authority over the workings of Grand
Lodge while it is in recess and it would be inconsistent with that power to allow a
Committee to make a decision which he cannot reverse.
As the Grand Master probably already has the power to do what the
resolution seeks to accomplish it is prudent to spell it out in the Code.
For the reasons stated, the Committee is of the opinion that this
clarification of the Code is constructive and well taken and therefore recommends
a yes vote on the resolution.
One member of the Committee recused himself from the vote on this
resolution because he is one of the proponents of the resolution.
Resolution CARRIED-OVER.
Resolution No. 14-02
Makes a Correction to Resolution 11-13
The proponents of this Resolution seek to correct Resolution 11-13 by excluding
members present who are not in good standing from the count of the members
required for the lodge to act.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, Resolution 11-13 added the requirement that only
members whose dues are current (that is, members who are in good standing)
may participate in lodge business; and

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

221

WHEREAS, all questions in lodge are decided by a vote or ballot of
the members present, which would include members present who are not in good
standing; and
WHEREAS, this rule should be corrected to provide that all questions
in lodge shall be decided by a vote or ballot of the members present who are also
in good standing.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Section 807.020 of
the California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§807.020. ADDITIONAL REGULATIONS APPLICABLE TO MEETINGS.
A.

Sunday Meetings. No Stated or Special Meetings of a Lodge shall be
held on Sunday except for the annual Installation of Officers or funeral
services. If the Stated Meeting of a lunar Lodge falls on a Sunday, the
Stated Meeting shall be held on the following day.

B.

Work to be Done in Lodge of Entered Apprentice Masons. All business,
except examinations in the Candidate’s Lecture of the Fellow Craft and
Master Mason degrees, the conferring of the Fellow Craft and Master
Mason degrees, and the consideration of relief of a worthy Mason, shall
be done in a Lodge of Entered Apprentice Masons. At the option of the
retiring Master, the Lodge may be opened either on the First Degree or
on the Third Degree for the purpose of installing officers. A Lodge of
Master Masons may be called down for examinations in the Candidate’s
Lecture of the Entered Apprentice and Fellow Craft degrees. A Lodge
of Fellow Craft Masons may be called down for examinations in the
Candidate’s Lecture of the Entered Apprentice degree. At a Stated
Meeting, the Lodge may be called up for examinations in the Candidate’s
Lecture of the Fellow Craft and Master Mason degrees.

C.

Quorum. A Lodge shall not be opened, nor shall any work be done
or business transacted, except by, or in the presence of, and under the
continual direction of the Master, the ranking Warden, the Grand Master
or the Grand Master’s designated representative. No Lodge shall transact
any business with fewer than five members of the Lodge present except
the conferring of degrees. The Tiler is present while he is at his post in
the Tiler’s room.

D.

Presence of Charter. No meeting shall be conducted by a Lodge unless
the Charter of the Lodge is present. A photocopy of the Charter may
be made under the direction of the Grand Secretary at the request
and expense of the Lodge. The Grand Secretary shall attach thereto a
certificate with the seal of Grand Lodge affixed that the copy is a true
copy of the Lodge’s Charter. The copy may be used by the Lodge instead
of the original Charter at any time.

222

Proceedings of the

E.

Presence of Flag. The Flag of our country shall be displayed at all
meetings of a Lodge. At the annual election of officers, and at such other
meetings as may be deemed desirable by the Master, the Flag shall be
formally presented at the Altar and received in the manner prescribed in
the Ritual. The Altar of a Lodge shall not be decorated with any flag.

F.

No Smoking. Smoking is forbidden in the Lodge room at all times when
the Lodge is in session.

G.

No Adjourned Meetings. There shall be no adjourned meeting. Each
meeting of a Lodge must be closed when the business proposed for
transaction has been concluded, but in no event later than the close of the
day on which it was opened.

H.

Good Standing Requirement. No member may make a motion, second
a motion, speak on a motion, vote on a motion, recommend anyone for
membership or ballot on membership at a Lodge meeting unless he is
then a member in good standing of that Lodge. He must present a current
dues receipt to the Tiler to demonstrate that he is a member of the Lodge
in good standing or be verified by the Master, Senior Warden, Junior
Warden, Secretary or Assistant Secretary as a member of the Lodge in
good standing. If a member is present who is not in good standing, any
question or action to be decided hereunder by a majority or greater vote
of the members present shall be decided by a majority or greater vote of
the members present who are in good standing.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Article IV of Section 802.020 of
the California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
ARTICLE IV
AMENDMENTS
Section 1. Those portions of these Bylaws relating to the day and time of Stated
Meetings and the amount of fees and dues may be amended at any Stated
Meeting by a two‑thirds vote of the members present who are in good standing.
All proposed amendments must be presented, in writing, at a preceding Stated
Meeting and written notice must be given to each Lodge member setting forth
the text of the proposed amendment and the date of the Stated Meeting at which
the vote is to be taken. It shall have no effect until approved by the Grand Master.
The Secretary of the Lodge shall note in the minutes of the Lodge the notice
of the proposed amendments when made. When transmitting an amendment for
approval, he shall forward a certificate, under seal, showing that the law has been
complied with and that the amendment has received the required vote.

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of this resolution seek to modify Section 807.020 of
the California Masonic Code to exclude members present at a Lodge meeting
who are not in good standing from the count of members required for the
Lodge to act.
Resolution 11-13 amended the CMC to exclude members not in good
standing from voting on Lodge business but did not change the method for
determining what constitutes a majority or greater vote. It is conceivable that
a situation could arise where a majority of members present have not yet paid
their dues (and are not in good standing), thus preventing the Lodge from
taking any action requiring a majority vote.
This resolution addresses this situation by defining the number of
members necessary to take action as being based solely on members present
who are in good standing.
This Resolution is consistent with the policy and general purposes of this
Grand Lodge.

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of this Resolution seek to amend the California
Masonic Code to allow Lodges to use the same system to determine their annual
dues for the upcoming Masonic year as does the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

225

F&AM of California. Article III of the CMC presently allows for a Lodge to
amend its By-Laws to provide for its annual dues in three (3) different ways .
Lodges have the ability to establish their annual dues either by a set amount;
or by set amount plus the Per Capita sum established by Grand Lodge at the
immediately preceding Annual Communication; or by a set amount plus the
Per Capita sum established by the Grand Lodge at the immediately preceding
Annual Communication, with the total thus determined rounded up to next
whole number. The proponents want to provide a Lodge an additional method
for setting the amount for annual dues without having to amend their By-Laws
each year and may forego small changes in dues that may create budgeting
issues. A Lodge using this method would have to adopt its budget prior to
sending out dues notices, which would usually require the budget adoption to
occur in the fall preceding the new fiscal year.
The Grand Lodge, for many years, has attempted to create an
atmosphere to assist local Lodges in managing their affairs in simpler terms
so as not to create too much confusion. This Resolution would provide the
constituent Lodges with additional ways to set the amount for their annual
dues without having to go through the process of amending their By-Laws . It
would require the Lodge to provide projections of expenditures, income, and
the number of dues paying members.
This Resolution is consistent with the policy and general purposes of
this Grand Lodge.

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of this Resolution seek to have a new trial in Trial
Number 2006.
California Masonic Code Section 1404.1000 provides the procedure
for the request of an expelled Mason to be restored to membership. The 2009
Grand Master Decision Number 3, approved by this Grand Lodge, set forth a
detailed set of criteria to be considered when determining whether an expelled
member has demonstrated rehabilitation from his past conduct and that his
reinstatement would not be contrary to our Masonic principles. These criteria
include the likelihood that he will not repeat the conduct which gave rise to
the expulsion, his acceptance of responsibility, remorse and atonement for his
conduct, and change in attitude. The Decision specifically requires him to provide
evidence of his rehabilitation from his past misconduct. This expelled man has not
satisfied these criteria.
This Resolution seeks to bypass this established procedure for
reinstatement. There is no precedent for a verdict affirmed by Grand Lodge to be
overturned. This trial has come before this Grand Lodge on several occasions and
the Trial Review Committee has recommended each time to uphold the verdict of
the trial commission and the vote of Grand Lodge concurred.
Furthermore, the deadline imposed for the new trial by this resolution,
namely December 31, 2014, is virtually impossible to meet.
This resolution is not consistent with the policy and general purposes of
this Grand Lodge.
Report of the Committee on Trial Review:
Resolution 14-04 seeks to order a new trial in Trial Matter #2006 on
various grounds. The individual who is the subject of this resolution was expelled
in 2011 after a Trial Commission found that he had started a fight with another
brother, hitting him in the face, and that a civil suit against the Accused and the
residential park where he lived was later settled by payment of $45,000 to the
injured brother; the Accused was also involved in continuous, deliberate and
malicious acts against a neighbor in a Masonic community in which the Accused
lived, including operating a noisy mosquito abatement machine 24 hours a day
which was later abated by a Superior Court order which the Accused further
violated by destroying a hedge on the neighbor’s property, continually coming on
to the property in violation of the order, kicking down a barrier constructed by the
neighbor and violently hurling pieces of it against their residence and continually
confronting and harassing the neighbor, at one point telling her she was not

228

Proceedings of the

“welcome here” (she is of East Indian ancestry); the Trial Master also found that
the Accused and his supporters had harassed and intimidated witnesses to the
point that some were afraid to appear at the trial; at the time of trial the Accused
showed absolutely no remorse for any of his behavior.
This is the fourth time in four years this matter has been brought before
Grand Lodge - the trial was reviewed twice, once in 2011 and once in 2012, and
the decision to expel the member was affirmed by this Grand Lodge both times.
On the second occasion the Accuser filed an argument with the Committee which
did not conform to the requirements of our Code and therefore had to be rejected
by the Committee.
In 2013 the matter was again before this Grand Lodge pursuant to a
request for restoration. This Committee reported that the request did not even
come close to complying with the requisites set forth in the Masonic Code for
restoration and therefore recommended the request be denied. This Grand Lodge
agreed and rejected the request.
Now the proponents of this resolution seek to make an end run around
the Masonic Code by asking the Grand Lodge to disregard all the procedural
safeguards built into the Code and to order a new trial despite the fact that this
Grand Lodge has reviewed the matter on three separate occasions and rejected the
request each time. This resolution presents no new information not included in
their prior attempts to overturn the verdict.
Our Code provides strict guidelines for the review of Masonic trials
designed to insure both the Accuser and the Accused receive due process and a
fair result. Those procedures were complied with by this Grand Lodge three times
but now the proponents of this resolution ask the Grand Lodge to ignore the Code
and to give them a third bite at the apple. By passing this resolution Grand Lodge
would be granting this expelled member an unprecedented remedy not recognized
by our Masonic Code; as such, it would be the antithesis of the equal justice which
Masonry stands for.
The reasons set forth in the resolution are filled with mis-statements of
fact, glaring omissions from the trial record and statements which can only be
generously characterized as speculation. Moreover, because of the nature of the
vehicle they chose to present their argument the Accuser was unable to respond to
the allegations they make in their resolution.
The charges of a “kangaroo” court and a “white hat conspiracy” have
been thoroughly investigated by the Committee and rejected as there is no basis
in fact for them. The claim that a member of the Committee on Trial Review who
was involved in the case at the trial voted on the review of the case is a blatant
falsehood as the Grand Lodge proceedings record the fact that it was reported that
the member of the committee involved recused himself from the vote. And the

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

229

request that the matter be re-tried before December of this year presents Grand
Lodge with a factual impossibility as it will be impossible to appoint a trial master,
commissioners and further comply with the procedural requirements of the Code
as well as calendaring a trial within that period of time.
In sum, if Grand Lodge were to pass this resolution it would set a precedent
allowing anyone aggrieved by the decision of a Masonic Trial Commission to
bypass our review process and the Committee on Trial Review and to appeal
directly to Grand Lodge based on allegations to which the opposing party cannot
respond and thus render ineffectual the statutory scheme which this Grand Lodge
has spent many years refining in a desire to render both sides of a controversy due
process. The proponents of this resolution could better spend their time seeking
restoration of this individual pursuant to the Code by establishing his rehabilitation
and reformation relative to the conduct for which he was originally expelled.
For the reasons stated, the Committee therefore recommends a no vote
on the resolution.
One Member of the Committee recused himself from the vote on
this resolution.

§406.060. MASONIC PROPERTIES.

Any option or contract for the purchase of real property, except a contract

the expected cost is not in excess of $15,000 during any calendar year;

B.

The encumbrance of real property;

C.

The lease of real property, as lessor or lessee, for more than three years;

D.

A contract for or commencement of the construction, alteration,
improvement, replacement, repair, or maintenance of real property if the
expected cost is in excess of $25,000; and

E.

Any option or contract regarding the sale or listing for sale of
real property.

The committee shall, subject to the approval of the Grand Master, establish rules
and regulations governing the processing of applications for committee approval.
The committee shall review the reports of transactions of Masonic Hall
Associations submitted to the Grand Secretary as provided in Section 900.050
of this Code and may give counsel and advise concerning the operation of those
Masonic Hall Associations.
The committee shall also advise Lodges and the Grand Lodge on matters of
taxation with respect to income, property, sales and employment taxes.

§809.130. LODGE INVESTMENTS.
Exclusive of a Lodge investment in an incorporated Masonic Hall Association,

Proceedings of the
For purposes of this Code, cemetery property shall mean an entire
cemetery, a cemetery parcel, an exclusive section within a cemetery,
and an individual cemetery plot, crypt, niche or other interment right.
For purposes of this Code, cemetery property shall be considered
real property.

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
Over the past several years, Lodges throughout this jurisdiction have
become recipients of cemetery property. A committee was formed in 2012 to
standardize cemetery property management and the results of its deliberations
led to a number of proposed resolutions that were submitted for the 2013
Annual Communication. As has already been seen, some of those resolutions
were carried over until 2014.
One of those resolutions, 13-22, did not achieve a majority vote and
was defeated in 2013. The intent of that resolution was to provide the details
of how lodges could acquire cemetery property. However, in order to prevent
lodges from speculating in such property, a number of complicated restrictions
were part of that resolution. The proponents have now introduced Resolution
14-05, which removes much of this language.
Under these new provisions, two sections of our code, 406.060,
which deals with Masonic Properties, and 809.130, which deals with Lodge
Investments, are amended, and a new section, 809.160, dealing specifically with
Masonic Cemetery Property, is created. If this resolution passes, a lodge would
be permitted to purchase cemetery property without Grand Lodge approval if
no more than a total of $15,000 is spent each year; Grand Lodge approval is
required for larger sums. The Lodge may also receive cemetery property as
donations. However, the cemetery property must be in the name of the Lodge
and not any other person or body, including a Hall Association. Grand Lodge
must be informed of such purchases and donations and will maintain a listing
of all cemetery property owned by lodges throughout the jurisdiction.
The Lodge may use cemetery property for interring eligible Masons
or eligible Masonic relatives if financial circumstances require such actions.
The Lodge may also sell the property to any person at its discretion, with
the proceeds being placed in its general funds. Again, Grand Lodge has to be
informed of any such use or sale of the property.
Since it is the obligation of Masons to accept responsibility for the
interment needs of other Masons, their widows and orphans, this resolution is
consistent with the policy and general purposes of this Grand Lodge.
Resolution CARRIED-OVER.

Resolution No. 14-06
Standardizes Candidates Coaching Program
The proponents of this Resolution seek to standardize the candidates
coaching program.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, candidate coaching varies from lodge to lodge; and
WHEREAS, candidate coaching and its management is vital to a
successful lodge; and
WHEREAS, page 5 of the online version of the Lodge Manual merely
“recommends” that the duties of the Senior Warden include (1) responsibility
for the coaching of all candidates; (2) selection of qualified brothers to coach
candidates; (3) ensuring that Candidates Coaches Handbooks are available for
all Candidate’s Coaches; (4) ensuring that all candidates are progressing at a
reasonable rate; and (5) regular updates to the Candidates Record Book; and
WHEREAS, page 16 of the online version of the Lodge Manual merely
“recommends” appointment by the Master of a Candidates Coaching Committee
to provide each newly initiated, passed or raised brother with a proficient
instructor; and
WHEREAS, page 16 of the online version of the Lodge Manual merely
“recommends” that the Candidates Coaching Committee should consist of at least
four members, one for each of the degrees and the Head Candidates’ Coach who
oversees the work of the others; and
WHEREAS, the California Masonic Code is silent on this vitally
important candidate management function; and
WHEREAS, the Fraternity would greatly benefit by including the
management of candidate coaching in the California Masonic Code.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Section 805.210 of
the California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§805.210. DUTIES OF WARDENS.
It shall be the duty of the Wardens to assist the Master in the performance of
his duties, and to discharge all those duties which ancient usage has assigned to
their respective stations. Working with the Candidates Coaching Committee, the
Senior Warden shall be responsible for seeing that (a) each candidate is receiving

236

Proceedings of the

coaching; (b) each coach has available the Candidates Coaches Handbook; (c)
each candidate is progressing at a reasonable rate; and (d) the Candidates Record
Book is kept current. During the absence of the Master, the Senior Warden, and
in his absence the Junior Warden, shall succeed to and be charged with all the
powers and duties of the Master.

Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§806.000. COMMITTEES.

The Master, at the Stated Meeting next succeeding his installation, shall

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of this Resolution seek to standardize the candidates
coaching program. For many decades, prior to the shortening of the first and
second Degree proficiencies, nearly all Lodges in this Jurisdiction did precisely
what the proponents are asking.
The Senior Warden, or in his absence the Junior Warden, was in charge
of the candidates coaching. Every brother knew that on becoming Senior Warden,
it would be his responsibility to supervise the coaching of new members. Today,
most Lodges ignore the recommendation of the current Lodge Manual as it
relates to the duties of the Senior Warden and his leadership of the candidates
coaching program.
This Resolution will restore a time-honored program to our Lodges
and give far more information and knowledge to our new members.
This Resolution is consistent with the policy and general purposes of
this Grand Lodge.

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of this Resolution seek to amend the rules on personal
identifying information to an opt-out rule.
Section 810.040 of the California Masonic Code requires members
to affirmatively consent in writing that their personal identifying information
may be used in the public domain. This requirement resulted in numerous
administrative problems because the Lodge had to obtain permission from
each member. This resolution will amend the CMC by requiring members to
notify the lodge in writing that they want their information withheld. This will
substantially ease the administrative burden of the Lodge.
This resolution is consistent with the policy and general purposes of
this Grand Lodge.

Resolution No. 14-08
Modifies Procedures Applicable to Grand Lodge Review of Trials
The proponents of this Resolution seek to add notifications to involved parties
when additional material is filed with the Committee on Trial Review and when
the Committee recommends any change in the verdict or penalty.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, currently the California Masonic Code allows for proper
notification of charges filed, time for response, notification of verdict and
submission of evidence, to name a few; and
WHEREAS, safeguards are also present within the California Masonic
Code which provide a secondary review similar to an appeals process by which
the Committee on Trial Review can review whether the verdict is supported by
substantial evidence or should be modified for good cause or in the interest of
justice; and

240

Proceedings of the

WHEREAS, safeguards are not present in the California Masonic Code
protecting the interest of the Accused or the Accuser when the Committee on Trial
Review recommends overturning or changing of a verdict; and
WHEREAS, this Resolution provides the Trial Master, the Accused and
the Accuser an opportunity to provide written responses to additional evidence
and arguments filed in accordance with Section 1404.910.C of the California
Masonic Code and notice to concerned parties of the Annual Communication at
which the Committee report will be acted upon.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Section 1404.910 of
the California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§1404.910. GRAND LODGE REVIEW.
All trial records under Chapters 3 and 4 of this Part 14 shall be reviewed by Grand
Lodge, as follows:
A.

All trial records received by the Grand Secretary under this chapter or
under Chapter 3 of this part shall be forwarded by him to the Committee
on Trial Review for review.

B.

If in the opinion of a majority of the members of the Committee on Trial
Review a verdict of guilty and/or a penalty is not supported by substantial
evidence, the Committee may postpone the effectiveness of the penalty
pending Grand Lodge action on the trial record. The committee may take
this act with or without a request from the Accused.

C.

If either an Accused or Accuser desires to have any evidence considered
that could not have been produced before the verdict was rendered, a
written statement setting forth the substance of such evidence and
explaining why it was not produced before the verdict was rendered may
be filed with the Grand Secretary not later than 60 15 days prior to the
commencement of the next Annual Communication of Grand Lodge.
Any arguments or representations which the Accused, the Accuser, or
any other Mason desires to present must be in writing and filed with the
Grand Secretary not later than 60 15 days prior to the commencement of
the next Annual Communication of Grand Lodge. The Grand Secretary
shall forward copies of any such filings to the Trial Master and the
opposing party or parties within 5 days of their receipt. Each of the
Trial Master and any opposing party may file a written response to any
such filings with the Grand Secretary not later than 15 days prior to the
commencement of the next Annual Communication of Grand Lodge.

D.

The Committee on Trial Review shall examine each trial record
together with such statements or arguments in writing, if any, as may be
presented and shall report its recommendations at the next succeeding
Annual Communication.

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

241

1.

The Committee shall review the record to determine whether
the verdict is supported by substantial evidence. All evidentiary
conflicts and all legitimate and reasonable inferences that may
be drawn from the trial record shall be in favor of sustaining
the verdict. Where the evidence supports more than one
inference, the Committee may not substitute its determination
in place of the determinations made by the trier of fact. The
Committee may recommend that the verdict be overturned
only if the verdict is not supported by substantial evidence. If
the Committee recommends that the verdict be overturned, it
shall include in its report the specific facts contained in the trial
record upon which it makes such recommendation.

2.

Based on its review of the record, the Committee may
recommend that the penalty be modified for good cause and
in the interest of justice. If the Committee recommends that
the penalty imposed should be modified in any respect, it shall
include in its report the specific facts contained in the trial
record upon which it makes such recommendation.

3.

When the Committee recommends to Grand Lodge that a
verdict and/or the penalty recommended by the Trial Master
be modified, the Accuser shall be notified in writing of such
recommendation, by registered mail return receipt requested,
not later than 30 days prior to the commencement of the
Annual Communication of the Grand Lodge at which such
recommendation shall be considered.

E.

After receipt of the report of the Committee on Trial Review, Grand
Lodge may affirm, modify, or reverse the verdict and/or penalty, remand
the matter to the Trial Master with instructions or make such other order
as it deems proper. The Grand Secretary shall send a copy of the Grand
Lodge action to the Trial Master as soon as possible. Without the consent
of the Accused, Grand Lodge may not affirm the verdict and/or penalty
until a period of forty-five days has elapsed since the Grand Secretary’s
notification to the Accused under Section 1404.630 of this Code.

F.

Pending Grand Lodge action on the trial record, no Lodge may take
action upon the restoration of a Mason under penalty of suspension.

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of this Resolution seek to increase the time an Accused
or Accuser has to respond to additional evidence provided to the Committee
on Trial Review following a Masonic Trial. Currently, such additional evidence
must be filed with the Grand Secretary at least 15 days prior to the next Annual
Communication of Grand Lodge following the trial. This Resolution would

242

Proceedings of the

change that to 60 days and would also require the Grand Secretary to forward
copies of all evidentiary requests to the Trial Master and opposing party. Any
response from the Trial Master or opposing party would be due no later than
15 days before the Annual Communication.
This Resolution would further require that the Accuser-but not the
Accused-be notified in writing by registered mail at least 30 days before the
Annual Communication if the Committee on Trial Review recommends to
Grand Lodge that a verdict be overturned or that the penalty recommended by
the Trial Master be modified.
It is the policy of this Grand Lodge to provide due process to the
Accused and Accuser alike throughout the proceedings of a Masonic Trial.
Since this Resolution would not provide equal notice to the Accuser and the
Accused, it is not consistent with the policy and general purposes of this
Grand Lodge.
Report of the Committee on Trial Review:
California Masonic Code §1404.910(C) provides that after a trial either
party may file with the Committee on Trial Review a written statement setting
forth any evidence which was not produced before the verdict was rendered
and the reasons it could not have been produced at trial for consideration by the
Committee in its review of the verdict.
The first proposed change requires the Grand Secretary to forward to
the Trial Master and the parties in the trial copies of any documents filed with the
Committee on Trial Review. This is the procedure which is presently followed by
the Committee on Trial Review. The resolution also requires that this be done no
later than sixty (60) instead of the current fifteen (15) days before Grand Lodge. A
response, if any, to such filing must be filed no later than fifteen (15) days before
Grand Lodge.
In a later paragraph of the resolution the proponents wish to mandate
that if a recommendation by the Committee on Trial Review is for a change in
the verdict or penalty it must be reported to only the Accuser thirty (30) days
prior to Grand Lodge. There are two preeminent problems with this proposal: 1)
by requiring the Committee to issue a recommendation fifteen days before the
opponent of any newly discovered evidence has to file their response thereto it
precludes the Committee from considering any documents filed in opposition to
the request and 2) the thirty day requirement serves no purpose since no other
filings are permitted after the recommendation is issued, therefore, the parties
could not legally respond to the recommendation nor could Trial Review modify
its recommendation.

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

243

There are also a number of other problems with the proposal. First, by
requiring that only the Accuser be notified the Accused is kept in the dark relative
to the Committee’s recommendation. That is inconsistent with other provisions
of our Code which promote full disclosure and no communications with either
party without the other one being privy to them. Second, the requirement
would only be invoked if the verdict is proposed to be modified but is silent
if the recommendation is to reverse the verdict. There seems to be no reason
apparent for the distinction. It appears that the only purpose of this recommended
legislation would be to allow the Accuser, and the Accuser alone, to be privy to
the Committee’s recommendation well in advance of Grand Lodge so that he can
engage in a lobbying effort; that would constitute an ex parte communications
with the Committee or electioneering, both of which would be improper.
Lastly, and more importantly, the resolution if passed would impose
restrictions on the Committee which are overly burdensome and unworkable. The
process the Committee has utilized for many years is that as trial records are
sent to it by the Grand Secretary they are disseminated to the members of the
Committee who review them, the Chairman then assigns one member to report
to the Committee on each trial and then the reports are disseminated to the other
members of the Committee. The reports are then discussed by telephone and
Email and the Committee meets just prior to the annual communication. At that
time the trial records are discussed again and a vote is taken on each case.
Requiring the Committee to disclose recommendations thirty days before
the annual communication would require the Committee to meet, in person, 90 to
120 days before Grand Lodge. That meeting would have to be at Grand Lodge as
that is where the originals of the trial records are kept. To meet that early before
Grand Lodge would be impracticable as many of the trial records do not arrive at
Grand Lodge that early and are not sent to the Committee that early. The result
would be that many cases would not be heard in a timely fashion and would be
delayed for a year and the cut-off would be something in the neighborhood of 5
– 6 months before Grand Lodge, thus giving the Committee only the opportunity
to review a half a year’s cases. And, lastly, the Committee would not have the
opportunity to consider the documents filed by anyone responding to a new
evidence filing.
The point of meeting and making determinations at Grand Lodge is
multifold: 1) the Committee is able to review and vote on all of the trial records,
even those which arrive late; 2) the cost to Grand Lodge for the members of
the Committee to travel to San Francisco for an additional meeting would be
substantial and beyond the Committee’s budget; 3) the announcement of the
Committee’s recommendations at Grand Lodge is designed to minimize the
opportunity for the parties interested in a case to lobby members of the Committee
for a particular vote.

244

Proceedings of the

In sum, this resolution would put the Committee in an impossible position
and would ultimately prevent some cases from being heard at Grand Lodge as
they are under our present system thereby causing further causing distress to the
parties and continuing disharmony in the lodge.
While the Committee is in favor of the recommended revision of the
Code as to notifying the parties of appellate documents having been filed, it
cannot recommend for approval the balance of the legislation which will cause
considerable harm to the function of this Grand Lodge.
For the reasons stated, the Committee therefore recommends a no vote
on the resolution.
Resolution NOT ADOPTED.

To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, more than 100 years ago, Masons from throughout the

Resolution No. 14-12
Allows Business in Any Degree Unless an
Entered Apprentice or Fellow Craft is Present
The proponents of this Resolution seek to allow for the conduct of Lodge business
in any degree unless an Entered Apprentice or Fellow Craft is present.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, since adoption of Resolution 11-06, California Lodges
have been strengthened by the participation of Entered Apprentice Masons and
Fellow Craft Masons in Lodge business meetings; and
WHEREAS, since adoption of Resolution 11-06, it is now uncommon
for our Lodges to work in a Lodge of Fellow Craft Masons or in a Lodge of
Master Masons; and
WHEREAS, since adoption of Resolution 11-06, many Lodges have
become less proficient in the rituals of the Fellow Craft and Master Mason
degrees; and
WHEREAS, it is generally accepted that the quality of our ritual
proficiency is proportional to the amount of practice and exposure members have
to that ritual work; and
WHEREAS, Masons of all degrees are edified by instruction, discussion,
and ritual practice in all of the degrees that they have received; and
WHEREAS, it is not appropriate to hold Masonic Communication,
education, or practice regarding the Fellow Craft or Master Mason rituals in a
Lodge of Entered Apprentice Masons; and
WHEREAS, other jurisdictions currently allow Masonic business to
be conducted on any degree of Masonry that all members in attendance have
received; and
WHEREAS, our current California Masonic Code already grants to
retiring Masters the option of opening Lodge on either the First or Third degree
when meeting for the purpose of installing officers; and

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

247

WHEREAS, allowing the Master the additional discretion of conducting
our Stated Meetings on any degree of Masonry that all members in attendance
have received will not exclude any Mason from attending any business meeting
that they are otherwise already entitled to attend; and
WHEREAS, this Resolution, if adopted, will afford all Lodge members
the opportunity to remain fluent in the ceremonies of all the degrees they have
received, and result in increased breadth and depth of our Masonic discussions,
while introducing no new restriction on any Mason who desires to attend
our meetings.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Section 807.020 of
the California Masonic Code be amended as marked:
§807.020. ADDITIONAL REGULATIONS APPLICABLE TO MEETINGS.
A.

Sunday Meetings. No Stated or Special Meetings of a Lodge shall be
held on Sunday except for the annual Installation of Officers or funeral
services. If the Stated Meeting of a lunar Lodge falls on a Sunday, the
Stated Meeting shall be held on the following day.

B.

Work to be Done in Lodge of Entered Apprentice Masons. All business,
except examinations in the Candidate’s Lecture of the Fellow Craft and
Master Mason degrees, the conferring of the Fellow Craft and Master
Mason degrees, and the consideration of relief of a worthy Mason, shall
be done in a Lodge of Entered Apprentice Masons. At the option of the
retiring Master, the Lodge may be opened either on the First Degree or
on the Third Degree for the purpose of installing officers. A Lodge of
Master Masons may be called down for examinations in the Candidate’s
Lecture of the Entered Apprentice and Fellow Craft degrees. A Lodge
of Fellow Craft Masons may be called down for examinations in the
Candidate’s Lecture of the Entered Apprentice degree. At a Stated
Meeting, the Lodge may be called up for examinations in the Candidate’s
Lecture of the Fellow Craft and Master Mason degrees. If the presiding
officer determines that there are no Entered Apprentices present for the
opening of a Lodge of Entered Apprentice Masons for the purpose of
holding a Stated Meeting, he may at his option hold the Stated Meeting
in a Lodge of Fellow Craft Masons. If the presiding officer determines
that there are no Entered Apprentices or Fellow Crafts present for the
opening of a Lodge of Entered Apprentice Masons for the purpose of
holding a Stated Meeting, he may at his option hold the Stated Meeting
in a Lodge of Fellow Craft Masons or in a Lodge of Master Masons.

C.

Quorum. A Lodge shall not be opened, nor shall any work be done
or business transacted, except by, or in the presence of, and under the
continual direction of the Master, the ranking Warden, the Grand Master
or the Grand Master’s designated representative. No Lodge shall transact

248

Proceedings of the
any business with fewer than five members of the Lodge present except
the conferring of degrees. The Tiler is present while he is at his post in
the Tiler’s room.

D.

Presence of Charter. No meeting shall be conducted by a Lodge unless
the Charter of the Lodge is present. A photocopy of the Charter may
be made under the direction of the Grand Secretary at the request
and expense of the Lodge. The Grand Secretary shall attach thereto a
certificate with the seal of Grand Lodge affixed that the copy is a true
copy of the Lodge’s Charter. The copy may be used by the Lodge instead
of the original Charter at any time.

E.

Presence of Flag. The Flag of our country shall be displayed at all
meetings of a Lodge. At the annual election of officers, and at such other
meetings as may be deemed desirable by the Master, the Flag shall be
formally presented at the Altar and received in the manner prescribed in
the Ritual. The Altar of a Lodge shall not be decorated with any flag.

F.

No Smoking. Smoking is forbidden in the Lodge room at all times when
the Lodge is in session.

G.

No Adjourned Meetings. There shall be no adjourned meeting. Each
meeting of a Lodge must be closed when the business proposed for
transaction has been concluded, but in no event later than the close of the
day on which it was opened.

H.

Good Standing Requirement. No member may make a motion, second
a motion, speak on a motion, vote on a motion, recommend anyone for
membership or ballot on membership at a Lodge meeting unless he is
then a member in good standing of that Lodge. He must present a current
dues receipt to the Tiler to demonstrate that he is a member of the Lodge
in good standing or be verified by the Master, Senior Warden, Junior
Warden, Secretary or Assistant Secretary as a member of the Lodge in
good standing.

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of this Resolution seek to allow Lodges to conduct
Stated Meetings in a Lodge of Master Masons, a Lodge of Fellow Craft
Masons, or a Lodge of Entered Apprentice Masons. Currently, Stated Meetings
must be conducted in a Lodge of Entered Apprentice Masons. This Resolution
would allow a Master of a Lodge to open on the lowest degree common to the
Brethren present at the opening of a Lodge for a Stated Meeting.
If only Master Masons are present at the opening of a Lodge for a
Stated Meeting, then this Resolution would allow the Master to conduct the
Stated Meeting in a Lodge of Master Masons, a Lodge of Fellow Craft Masons,
or a Lodge of Entered Apprentice Masons. If a Fellow Craft is present, then

Grand Lodge F. & A.M. of California

249

the Master would be allowed to conduct the Stated Meeting in a Lodge of
Fellow Craft Masons or a Lodge of Entered Apprentice Masons. If an Entered
Apprentice Mason is present, then the Master would be required to conduct
business in a Lodge of Entered Apprentice Masons.
This Resolution would not allow Lodges of Master Masons or Lodges
of Fellow Craft Masons to call down to accommodate a Mason who arrives
late and who desires admission.
It is the policy of this Grand Lodge to include Entered Apprentice
and Fellow Craft Masons in Stated Meetings. This Resolution would exclude
Entered Apprentice and Fellow Craft Masons who arrive late and desire
admission because they have not received the degree on which the Stated
Meeting is being conducted. As such, it is not consistent with the policy and
general purposes of this Grand Lodge.

§814.000. RESEARCH LODGES.
Research Lodges are a special classification of Constituent Lodge with authority
to conduct research, hold discussions, gather and preserve Masonic information,
maintain a library, supply papers or speakers at the request of other Lodges, and
conduct a program of general service to the Craft in the field of Masonic education

A.

The word “Research” shall be included in the name of the Lodge;

B.

Membership:
1.

Shall consist exclusively of Master Masons in good standing

Grand Lodges recognized by this Grand Lodge;

Proceedings of the
2.

Shall cease if a member loses such status; and

3.

May be voluntarily severed at any time by resignation;

No member of a Research Lodge shall, by reason of that membership

of this Code.
C.

Only Master Masons in good standing of a Constituent Lodge shall hold
office and vote;

D.

Grand Lodges recognized by this Grand Lodge, their Lodges and

Proceedings of the

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of this Resolution seek to allow Entered Apprentices
and Fellowcrafts to join Research Lodges but not to hold office or vote.
Research Lodges differ from Constituent Lodges in that they do not
confer degrees or have any judicial powers. Membership in a Research Lodge
is predicated on membership in a Constituent Lodge and does not entitle a
member to Masonic relief or any voting rights in Grand Lodge. Suspension
from a Research Lodge for non-payment of dues does not affect membership
in a Constituent Lodge.
Research Lodges perform a valuable function in California Freemasonry
by promoting Masonic education, and Entered Apprentices and Fellowcrafts
can benefit from membership without any adverse impact on Constituent Lodge
membership.
This Resolution is independent of Grand Master Recommendation 1403 and there is no apparent conflict between the two proposals.
This resolution is consistent with the policy and general purposes of
this Grand Lodge.

Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The proponents of Resolution No. 14-14 seek to add a Grand Historian
as an additional Grand Lodge Officer and specify the duties that this Officer
must perform. This Resolution would also require the Grand Lecturer, with the
approval of the Grand Master, to make the appropriate changes to applicable
Grand Lodge Ceremonies.
The Grand Lodge of California has existed for many years without a
Grand Historian; however the Grand Lodge staff has endeavored to accomplish
the preservation of historical artifacts throughout our Jurisdiction along with
managing our museum at the Grand Lodge building. Grand Lodge, through
the Institute for Masonic Studies, governs the Henry Wilson Coil Masonic
Library and Museum. It will be necessary to deconflict the duties of the Grand
Historian and Grand Lodge staff to avoid duplication of effort. The duties of
the Grand Historian will necessitate travel throughout the state, which will be
an additional expense for Grand Lodge.
However, it is within the purview of Grand Lodge to decide how best
to accomplish historical preservation, whether through a Grand Lodge officer,
Grand Lodge staff, or the efforts of individual lodges.
This Resolution is consistent with the policy and general purposes of
this Grand Lodge.
